name: The Weaver
summary: Giant spider ('mother of all eight-legs') in the Weaver's Chambers, in whose eye Silk's spear (Maligaro's Spike) is lodged; killed by the Exile.

name: Tibbs
summary: Brute-force and demolition rogue hireable in the Rogue Harbour. Running a contract with him unlocks Tullina.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_tibbs_the_giant", "locator": "Lead; \"To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs\" (Tullina page)"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_tullina_the_catburglar", "locator": "Lead: \"To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs, the Giant\""}]

name: Tolman
summary: Clarissa's lover, captured with her in the Slums and tortured to death by Piety of Theopolis in the Crematorium (Act 3); in Act 8 his zombie returns, and the failed resurrection at the Quay forces the exile to kill him.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_tolman", "locator": "Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_love_is_dead", "locator": "Walkthrough: Tolman attacks after the ritual fails"}]

name: Tor Gul, the Defiler
summary: Faridun boss of the Spires of Deshar, defeated before the Dreadnought assault.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest 'Defeat Tor Gul, the Defiler'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_2", "locator": "Progression table, The Spires of Deshar"}]

name: Tora, Master of the Hunt
summary: Forsaken master (ranged weapons); studied corruption in beasts. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Torvian, Hand of the Saviour
summary: Twilight Order champion and boss of Arastas in Act 4, defeated while the Exile searches for a way to reforge the Weapon.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_twilight_order", "locator": "Members"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "Arastas boss: Torvian, Hand of the Saviour"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Defeat Torvian, Hand of the Saviour"}]

name: Tujen, the Haggler / Harbourmaster
summary: Kalguuran haggler turned Kingsmarch harbourmaster who crews ships; former rebel who lost friends (Tolis, Oskar, Naja, Thea, Sven) and vows revenge; in PoE2 asks the Exile to clear the fog at Kedge Bay.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kingsmarch_shipping", "locator": "Tujen dialogue"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_letter_kingsmarch_", "locator": "Drunken Scrawl"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_dark_mists", "locator": "Tujen quote"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_expedition_league", "locator": "League mechanic: NPCs"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "Notable members: Current"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_dark_mists", "locator": "Tujen: 'Kingsmarch trade has seen better days'"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_1U2bFh1V9Mo", "locator": "[4:34] Tujen"}]

name: Tullina
summary: Agility rogue (the Catburglar). Her heist target is Merveil's Wedding Dress, which the History page ties to the Oriath wedding of Daresso and Merveil. Unlocked by a Tibbs contract; her contract unlocks Nenet.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_tullina_the_catburglar", "locator": "Lead: \"To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs, the Giant\""}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Daresso and Merveil' section: Merveil's wedding dress as a Heist target"}]

name: Tyndarus Phrecius
summary: Emperor c. 870-892 IC, backed by High Templar Andronicus; lost the Trarthan war of independence.

name: Uhtred
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1", "story_order": null}
summary: High Priest of the Order of the Chalice who declared the Vaal gems unclean, admitted responsibility for the attack on Olroth, and fled to an ancient shrine. Returns as the PoE1 boss Uhtred, Covetous Traitor.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Priesthood conspiracy; Aftermath"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "'===Thaumaturgy==='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "Notable members: Historical"}, {"source_id": "src_web_pcgamesn_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Tomb of Uhtred, the Stardrinker"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_grand_expedition", "locator": "step 49 'Defeat Uhtred, the Stardrinker'"}]

name: Ulaman, Sovereign of the Well
summary: Abyssal Lich, commander of the Lightless and servant of Kulemak. Boss of the Abyssal Depths (Abyss league 3.1.0).

name: Una
summary: Ezomyte Clearfell leader who helps the Exile free the Hooded One and sends them to recover Count Lachlann's ring.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_secrets_in_the_dark", "locator": "Quest 'Ask Una for help'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_mysterious_shade", "locator": "Quest 'Witness the revival of the Hooded One'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_recruit_the_ezomytes", "locator": "Speak to Una"}]

name: Undertaker Arimor
summary: Undertaker who gathers the haunted dead of Wraeclast, gives the Exile the Lantern of Arimor and runs the Necropolis; invokes a god named Thruldana during his chants.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_necropolis_league", "locator": "'==League mechanic==' Meet Undertaker Arimor"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_undertaker_s_apprentice", "locator": "tutorial quest"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "Thruldana entry"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "===Thruldana=== \"A god whose name is invoked by Undertaker Arimor during one of his chants.\""}]

name: Uromoti, Architect of Expansion
summary: Vaal Architect of Atziri who, per a carving in the Howling Caves, secretly built a vault in a remote mountain, hiding the 'treason' from the Queen and sending his children into it; his name is on a Temple Console medallion. Thought the Queen mad.

name: Ursea, The Matron
summary: Named in Act 5 datamine as a boss/text-audio entry. Unreleased; no lore available.

name: Utula
summary: Karui slave-rebellion leader and high priest of Kitava in Oriath; has Casticus's eyes taken to enter the Templar Courts, then uses Innocence's fall to complete the King's Feast and summon Kitava; killed by the Exile.

name: Uzaza, the First King
summary: Founder of the primeval civilisation who led his people on a migration in a cold winter; named on Uzaza's rings.

name: The Vaal Omnitect
summary: Vaal construct, boss of the present-day Temple of Atzoatl during the Incursion leagues; its exclusive currency drops come from it.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_incursion_league", "locator": "'Currency' / 'Unique items': 'The Vaal Omnitect, the boss of The Temple of Atzoatl'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'Constructs'"}]

name: Vagan, Weaponmaster
summary: Duelist forsaken master (weapons). Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Valdo Caeserius
summary: Chief Arkhon of the Oriath academy and father of Zana; dreamed of the Elder's dreamlands, was pulled into the Atlas, and fought the Elder until it ate his memories, becoming the Shaper. Aberration quotes show him grieving his Templar-killed wife.

name: Valerie, the Corsair
summary: Pondium-born corsair captain who borrowed the Sovereign from its masked, Templar-linked builders and freed Vesper's soul; recruits Exiles as first mates.

name: Vandroth, Blackblooded Enslaver
summary: Abyssal boss said by guides to drop Kulemak's Invitation (shared with Tasgul).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_timesaver_pinnacle_bosses", "locator": "Abyssal Commanders Tasgul and Vandroth drop Kulemak Invitation"}]

name: Varashta, the Winter Sekhema
summary: Former Maraketh Sekhema who projects herself near mirages and grants wishes; opposes Zarokh, the Grand Djinn of Time.

name: Vel Anxa
summary: Priest 'of the Order' listed as a Twilight Order member under Torvian, Hand of the Saviour. No further detail in sources read.

name: Velka, the Tide Witch
summary: Brinerot Shamanessa hunting the Allflame; boss in Kishara's Rest.

name: High Templar Venarius
summary: Puritanical High Templar who destroyed heretical texts and commissioned Valdo to assemble the Map Device; kidnapped Zana to force Valdo into the dreamlands, bargained with the Elder for power and was killed by it. In Synthesis he appears as a memory boss.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "'Notable members'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_shaper_quest", "locator": "Memory of Home / Intrigue / Grief"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Valdo Caeserius: 'Venarius tried to negotiate with the Elder ... it killed Venarius and his men'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_synthesis_league", "locator": "Boss list: Venarius"}]

name: Veritania, the Redeemer
summary: Scholar elderslayer who retreats into puritan disgust at the Atlas' vices and becomes the Redeemer.

name: Veruso, Prima Imperialus
summary: Eternal Empire figure who placed the Ankh of Eternity in a Quay shrine at the dawn of the Empire; his wife Chiara was changed by it.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_love_is_dead", "locator": "Clarissa: Veruso, Prima Imperialus, placed the Ankh; what it did to his wife Chiara"}]

name: Vesper
summary: Valerie's childhood friend whose body lies aboard the Sovereign while his soul is bound to the ship; runs Allflame crafting.

name: Vic Vox
summary: Victario 'Vic' Vox, one of the two Vox twin bosses of the Heist unique contract 'Contract: The Twins'. Member of the Vox family, descendant of Cardinal Sanctus Vox, named after the poet Victario. After Kurai steals the book 'O' Eternal' for a client he declares war on her, kidnaps and kills her cat Hana, and is killed with his twin by Kurai and the Exile.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_vic_vox", "locator": "lead and 'Lore' section"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kurai_the_administrator", "locator": "'The Negotiation', 'Returned To Rogue Harbour' and 'The Twins' sections"}]

name: Victario
aliases: ["The People's Poet", "Victario", "Victario Nevalius", "Victario Nevalius, the People's Poet"]
summary: A Sarn poet and art critic who joined the Purity Rebellion, created the Ancient Graffiti in Sarn, and led the uprisings in the Slums and Docks. At the Night of a Thousand Ribbons ambush he shouted 'Death to Sin!'. Central figure of the comic Path of Exile: Origins.

name: Vilenta
summary: Traitor who let Kitava's cultists into the Overseer's Tower; later a monster killed in the Control Blocks.

name: Vinderi
summary: Demolition and trap-disarmament rogue (the Dismantler) whose unique ability duplicates Heist chest contents. Unlocked by a Niles contract; his contract unlocks Gianna.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_vinderi_the_dismantler", "locator": "Lead and Heist ability; \"To unlock Vinderi, run a contract with Niles\""}]

name: Vinny Vox
summary: Vincent 'Vinny' Vox, twin brother of Vic Vox and co-boss of 'Contract: The Twins'. Descendant of Cardinal Sanctus Vox and member of the Vox family; the wiki states the Exile and Kurai kill both twins in the final contract.

name: Viper Napuatzi
summary: Vaal general of Utzaal's past who captures Alva and sends her to Doryani; defeated in the Utzaal time-gate sequence.

name: Volkuur, the Unbreathing Queen
summary: Boss of The Pale Court (Pale Council, Prophecy system); the wiki states the Pale Council fight no longer exists after 3.17.0. Drops Volkuur's Guidance.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_volkuur_the_unbreathing_queen", "locator": "Header: 'The prophecy system was removed from the game in version 3.17.0. The Pale Council fight no longer exists'; infobox location = The Pale Court; Drops: 'drops Volkuur's Guidance'"}]

name: High Templar Voll
aliases: ["Emperor Voll", "Emperor of Purity", "High Templar Voll", "Voll", "Voll of Thebrus", "Voll, Emperor of Purity"]
summary: High Templar who leads the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) against Chitus and becomes Emperor of the Eternal Empire. His reanimated remains in the Dried Lake are fought in Act 4.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_voll_emperor_of_purity", "locator": "Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Voll'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Purity Rebellion' and 'Reign of Voll'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "section 'Lore'"}]

name: Vorana
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1", "story_order": null}
summary: Black Scythe mercenary leader and Medved's beloved. She killed the twelve priests who stabbed Olroth, took gem-infused rites into her own flesh and left the walls. Returns as the boss Vorana, Last to Fall.

name: Vorici, Master Assassin
summary: Forsaken master (socket/colour crafting); Brotherhood of Silence member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Vornas, the Fell Flame
summary: Vornas, the Fell Flame is a boss the Exile defeats after passing the Galai Gates during the Recruit the Maraketh interlude.

name: Vruun, Marshal of Xesht
summary: PoE2 boss in Unstable Breaches, marshal serving Xesht; drops Lineage supports.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_vruun_marshal_of_xesht", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_vruun_marshal_of_xesht", "locator": "Version History: introduced in 0.5.0; boss in Unstable Breaches"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_gifts_for_the_genesis_tree", "locator": "The Head of Vruun"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_vruun_marshal_of_xesht", "locator": "lead and Drops"}]

name: Weylam Roth
summary: Undead pirate captain of the Black Crest, grandfather of Lilly Roth. Summoned by burning the Black Flag at the Beacon, he is bound to ferry the exile to the Brine King's Reef and on to Phrecia (Act 7); he later appears at the Bridge Encampment and the Oriath docks (Act 10), where he asks for Atziri's Elixir of Allure.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_brine_king_quest", "locator": "Weylam ferries to the reef"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kishara_s_star", "locator": "Weylam and Lilly"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_no_love_for_old_ghosts", "locator": "Weylam asks for the Elixir of Allure in the Ossuary"}]

name: Weylin
summary: Ezomyte slave poisoned by Chitus in the Labyrinth.

name: Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand
summary: Unique Breach monster (Atlas notable Call of Xesht-Ula, 3.17.0; no longer encounterable since 3.28.0) whose name is a portmanteau of the five Breachlords; summons apparitions of each lord and can drop any breachstone. The PoE2 wiki says the Breachlords had planned to merge into a being called Xesht-Ula. Not the same entity as Xesht.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_xesht-ula_the_open_hand", "locator": "lead + Trivia"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_dreamer", "locator": "Lore: Vaal Cult of the Purple Flame knew of the five Breachlords' plan to merge into Xesht-Ula"}]

name: Xibaqua
summary: Mythic/historical figure of the Vaal Empire whose remains were believed to be the progenitor of all Vaal; Vaal myth says their conflict with 'the gods' produced a 'droplet of pure light', the first Vaal. Unclear whether myth or history.

name: Xipocado, Royal Architect
summary: Atziri's Royal Architect who with Doryani rebuilt the temple as a self-modifying machine; boss in the Temple of Atzoatl (PoE1) and Atziri's Temple (PoE2).

summary: PoE2's three-trial system (Sekhemas, Chaos, and a planned third) that gates ascendancy. Each trial is tied to a Wraeclastian culture. Four tiers of trials give 2 ascendancy points each for 8 total.

name: The Atlas of Worlds (concept)
summary: The endgame structure of PoE1: a web of alternate worlds ('maps') reached through the Map Device. Wiki lore says it was either found or created by the Elder as a hunting ground; after the Elder's defeat other powers (Maven, Eldritch Horrors, the Originator) contest it. PoE2 has its own, separate Atlas whose Precursor Towers are mentioned in PoE1 wiki lore.

name: Atlas Passive Skill Tree
summary: The upgrade tree of the PoE1 Atlas endgame, spent with Atlas passive skill points and Atlas passive respec points. Points come from Atlas Book of Skill items and from quest rewards (for example The Elder, The Maven's Game, The Searing Exarch, The Eater of Worlds). The wiki counts 9 Atlas Books of Skill for 12 Atlas passive points in total.

name: Blight (fungal growth)
summary: Fungal growths infesting Wraeclast whose mycelium spawns monster waves once a Purification Pump pierces it. Cassia first thought it a symptom of Wraeclast's death, then a parasite, and suspects a central growth that Blighted maps lead to.

name: Blightheart
summary: Hypothesised original source of the Blight. Dhunan (historical Order of the Djinn 'Blightmaster') theorised its existence; Sister Cassia independently suspects a central growth that the Blighted maps lead to. No in-game confirmation is cited.

name: Bloodline modifier
summary: Bloodline modifiers were shared modifiers on each pack of magic monsters in Bloodlines league; they could affect combat while the pack lived and after it died.

name: The Breach
summary: Otherworldly realm/phenomenon whose tears let Breach monsters enter Wraeclast; original Breach league (2.5.0) had breaches expanding as monsters are killed, splinters forming Breachstones for the five Breachlords' Domains. Replaced in 3.28.0 by the Keepers-of-the-Flame rework (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree). PoE2 has Unstable Breaches and the Breachlords' lore (Xesht).

name: Imperial Seven-Day Week

name: Cataclysm
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "from the Precursor era to c. 1339 IC (several events)", "story_order": null}
summary: Lore term for the world-ending catastrophes that destroyed civilisations: the unknown cataclysm that wiped out the Precursors, the Vaal Cataclysm (also 'The Fall', c. 400 BIC), and the Eternal Empire Cataclysm (~1339 IC). The corpus uses the word for each event but does not define a single in-world category; this node groups those uses. Not the PoE2 epilogue quest 'Cataclysm's Wake', which is an Atlas tutorial quest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro: 'An incredibly advanced precursor civilization existed, but was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm.'; section '====The Vaal Cataclysm====': 'The Vaal Cataclysm, also known as The Fall, was a historical event...'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "section '===The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)===': 'The Cataclysm brought an end to Voll's reign and the Eternal Empire as a whole.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_cataclysm_s_wake", "locator": "page intro: 'Cataclysm's Wake is an epilogue quest. It act as the tutorial quest for the Atlas.'"}]

name: Citadels (Iron, Copper, Stone)
summary: Three Atlas fortresses (Iron, Copper, Stone) whose bosses drop one Crisis Fragment each toward the Arbiter of Ash: Iron Citadel = Count Geonor, Copper Citadel = Jamanra, Stone Citadel = Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge (agreed by several guides; the poe2 wiki Doryani page also lists the Stone Citadel). The removed 0.1-0.4 epilogue quests Faridun Foray (boss listed Count Geonor), Ezomyte Infiltration (boss listed The Perennial King) and Vaal Incursion (boss Doryani) all start 'Investigate the Burning Monolith'; how The Perennial King maps to Jamanra is unclear. Fragment mapping differs between guides.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_timesaver_poe2_citadels", "locator": "Citadel guide"}, {"source_id": "src_web_game8_arbiter_of_ash", "locator": "Iron=Ancient, Copper=Weathered, Stone=Faded per Game8"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_vaal_incursion", "locator": "quest infobox: boss Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge; start 'Investigate The Burning Monolith'; removed 0.5.0"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_faridun_foray", "locator": "quest infobox: boss Count Geonor; removed 0.5.0"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_ezomyte_infiltration", "locator": "quest infobox: boss The Perennial King; removed 0.5.0"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_doryani_royal_thaumaturge", "locator": "can be found in endgame as a citadel boss in The Stone Citadel"}, {"source_id": "src_web_timesaver_pinnacle_bosses", "locator": "Stone (Doryani), Copper (Jamanra), Iron (Count Geonor) - fragment mapping differs from other guides"}]

name: The Cleansing Fire
summary: Cosmic force: sentient neural network of suns and black stars seeking omniscience by disintegrating what it studies; served by the Black Star and the Searing Exarch. Its all-seeing-eye symbol resembles the descry and may be origin of Templar religion (wiki inference).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_cleansing_fire", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Lycia: 'prayed to symbol of the Cleansing Fire ... Innocence appropriated it'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_struggle", "locator": "Cleansing Fire section: 'omnipotent neural network of suns and black stars'; symbol 'very similar to the descry'"}]

name: Corruption
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "from the Precursor era onward (Beast, Vaal, Eternal Empire)", "story_order": null}
summary: Lore force of mutation and malformation tied to the Beast and its predecessors: the Beast 'possesses corrupting powers' that mutate whatever contacts it; Kitava is called 'God of Corruption' in Karui dialogue; Precursors mastered corruption and Doryani attempts to harness the Precursor Weapon to destroy corruption. Not the Corrupted-item mechanic.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_beast_lore", "locator": "intro: 'The Beast possesses corrupting powers, devouring the souls of his prey and mutating whoever comes in contact with it.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "section '==Kitava==' > Dialogue, Haku's 'Kaom' option: 'Kitava, God of Corruption, consumed Kaom from heart to skin.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section '===Precursor civilization===': 'After mastering corruption, they delved deeper...'; the Precursor Weapon is one 'which Doryani attempts to harness to destroy corruption'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "Haku dialogue: 'Kitava, God of Corruption'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "PoE2 section: 'the Seed of Corruption'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Vaal temple section: 'worship of Corruption'"}]

name: Crisis Fragments
summary: Fragments needed to open the sealed door of the Burning Monolith (Arbiter of Ash). In 0.1-0.4 three were needed (Ancient, Weathered, Faded), one per Citadel boss. In the 0.5 quest log only the Ancient and Weathered fragments are picked up in the Fortress Enigma Chambers; Citadels continue to drop them for repeat runs. Guides disagree on which Citadel drops which (most: Iron=Ancient, Copper=Faded, Stone=Weathered), and the quest log matches that for Geonor (Ancient) and Doryani (Weathered).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_pinnacle_of_flame", "locator": "Obtain three Crisis Fragments"}, {"source_id": "src_web_timesaver_poe2_citadels", "locator": "Citadel-to-Arbiter loop; fragment mapping disagrees between guides"}]

name: Darkness (Delve)
summary: Lightless darkness in the Azurite Mine that damages unprepared delvers; requires flares; Aul and Kurgal fights include a darkness phase.

name: Day Zero rule (league narrative)
summary: Dev narrative rule: each league story begins with the exile face-down on the Twilight Strand, just exiled by Dominus, so league events cannot build on what the exile did in earlier leagues. Earlier events are attributed to other exiles or remembered as memories.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule; cites 'Integrating League Stories' and ExileCon 2019 dev talks)"}]

name: Delirium
summary: Fog of madness released through Mirrors of Delirium that spawns and strengthens monsters and can lead to the Simulacrum. Origin is only hinted: Kalandra links it to 'the Trickster' and PoE2 ties Tangmazu to a tutorial Delirium encounter.

name: Delirium: The Hare and the Raven
summary: 0.5 Delirium storyline ('The Hare and the Raven' in the press release): Elder Madox is freed from a Delirium mirror (Strange Reflection), leads the Exile to the Withered Willow, and the Raven Trickster Tangmazu must be stopped. Official notes: 'An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed, spreading madness across Wraeclast.'
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Delirium (The Hare and the Raven): confrontation with Tangmazu"}, {"source_id": "src_web_domistae_poe2_endgame_guide", "locator": "Delirium"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_strange_reflection", "locator": "Quest log"}, {"source_id": "src_ggg_content_update_0_5_0", "locator": "An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed"}]

name: Doryani's contingencies
summary: Fan-synthesised reading of Doryani's secret preparations: anti-Beast Precursor weapon, flood-sealed Utzaal, and a time gateway needing Vaal blood. Interpretive; some details rest on tertiary YouTube analysis.

name: Essence
summary: Imprisoned essences freed in Essence league (2.4.0, Atlas of Worlds); modify items with guaranteed affixes; can be corrupted (Hysteria, Delirium, Horror, Insanity).

name: Exile (exile system)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "1599-1600 IC (PoE1); Trarthus precedent c. 870 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: The exile system: criminals of Oriath are sentenced by the Templar government and shipped to Wraeclast. The sentence text reads 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. The player's character is one of these exiles. Precedent exists: under Tyndarus Phrecius, people were exiled to the land later called Trarthus. The wiki gives no single in-world reason for choosing Wraeclast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_letters_of_exile", "locator": "section 'Format' (sentence template); exile entries 1597-1599 IC"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Present'; section 'Reign of Tyndarus Phrecius' (Trarthus exile)"}]

name: Exile's Journey (Day Zero rule)
summary: The wiki's 'Day Zero' rule: each league's narrative starts with the Exile face-down in the sand of the Twilight Strand, having just been exiled by Dominus, so league stories cannot build on earlier leagues' events.

name: Expedition and The Grand Expedition (PoE2)
summary: 0.5 Expedition storyline from Ruins of Kingsmarch: Rog searches for Gwennen across an ocean of islands, Medved, Vorana, Uhtred, Olroth lead factions; a Verisium meteor is the goal.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_grand_expedition", "locator": "quest log"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Expedition: Rog searches for his missing wife, Gwennen"}, {"source_id": "src_web_domistae_poe2_endgame_guide", "locator": "Expedition"}]

name: Ezomyte Runesmithing
summary: Rune craft with Kalguuran origins, revealed by Farrow in 0.5.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Farrow reveals the Kalguuran origins of Ezomyte Runesmithing"}]

name: Forsaken Masters
summary: Seven NPC masters introduced in Forsaken Masters (1.2.0): Elreon, Haku, Vorici, Vagan, Tora, Leo and Catarina (plus Zana); they vanished at Betrayal, taken by the Syndicate (all but Zana).

name: Fragmented Memory
summary: Decaying memory sub-zones found throughout Wraeclast in Synthesis; some are memories of real events (e.g. Malachai's slave mines, gemling experiments, the Templar Laboratory) and are used by the wiki as lore sources.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_synthesis_league", "locator": "League mechanic"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "citations of 'Abandoned Shaft Memory' and 'Eternal Residence Memory'"}]

name: Nature of godhood (ascension)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "before the creation of the Beast", "story_order": null}
summary: In PoE lore a mortal of rare quality could ascend to godhood on the adoration of their people, shedding mortality; this became impossible once Sin created the Beast. Becoming a god often costs one's humanity. Gods can also be 'made' by belief of followers (Innocence's ascension was fuelled by hatred of Sin).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'Ascension to godhood'"}, {"source_id": "src_ingame_sin_dialogue", "locator": "Sin, 'The Origins of the Gods': \"There was a time before the Beast ... men and women like you could ascend. Through rareness of quality and the adoration of their people...\""}]

name: Harbinger
summary: Otherworldly enemies of Harbinger league (3.0.0) beaten by killing their minions; drop currency shards.

name: Heart of the Grove
summary: Plant that grows from a harvested Tier 4 Sacred Grove seed (about 100 growth cycles). Harvesting it is the challenge that leads to the Avatar of the Grove; Oshabi herself turns into it after the tutorial quest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_harvest_league", "locator": "League mechanic: Heart of the Grove"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_oshabi", "locator": "Lead: Oshabi turns into the Heart of the Grove"}]

name: Eternal calendar
summary: Calendar of 1 IC (Imperialis Conceptus), seven days and thirteen moons (Verusi, Divini, Derivi ... Azmeri).

name: Eternal slave trade
summary: Under Chitus the Empire enslaved Karui, Ezomytes and Maraketh, sending them to mines and cities.

name: Intrinsic darkness
summary: Tane's term for the cruelty/ill-will in living beings that Metamorphs distil from monster organs; he now thinks it older and more universal than Corruption and hopes to destroy it while leaving the flesh unharmed.

name: Kalguuran runesmithing
summary: Kalguuran art of engraving starlight runes (Verisium from meteorites) into weapons and armour; Ezomytes learned it from the first expedition; revived as Runesmithing in Settlers and Runeforging in PoE2 Act 4.

name: Karui Gods
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "ancient; worshipped by the Karui", "story_order": null}
summary: The gods honoured within the Karui Way: Arohongui, Hinekora, Kitava, Ngamahu, Ramako, Tasalio, Tawhoa, Tukohama and Valako, as named on the Karui Gods page.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "intro: 'In the game's lore, The Karui Way has several gods that are representative of or rule over various aspects of the world.'"}]

name: Karui Way (Makanui)
summary: Karui code of honour and traditions (Way of the Warrior); some who follow it forbid virtue gems for causing blood fever.

name: The Kingsmarch Charter
summary: Royal charter under which Kingsmarch operates; Johan enforces it to the letter, including punishments such as the Royal Order of Criminal Hanging subject to a statute of limitations.

name: Kingsmarch shipping and trade routes
summary: Trade shipping from Kingsmarch to Kalguuran ports (Riben Fell, Pondium, Kalguur) and Karui ports (Ngakanu, Te Onui, Moti Aro); risks include pirates, corrupt officials, a royal tax and 'mysterious green light' losses. Pirate Admiral Valerius can commandeer ships.

name: Kingsmarch workers and town management
summary: Recruited workers (miners, smelters, farmers, disenchanters, shippers, Atlas runners) are hired through Raulf for Gold; the town runs on real-time resources: ores, bars, crops and thaumaturgic dust.

name: Leylines
summary: Ancient underground structures Doryani believes span the continent beneath the Ziggurat; they power the Waygate and resonate with the Precursor Tower.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Doryani: This Ziggurat was built over what my ancestors called 'leylines'"}]

name: Lifeforce
summary: Oshabi's name for the invisible force that revives the dead and shapes beasts and plants, released by Grove seeds in Wild, Vivid and Primal forms; she notes its similarity to Corruption and calls them perhaps 'two sides of the same leaf'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_oshabi", "locator": "Dialogue: Lifeforce, The Slaying of Malachai, Monsters"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_sacred_grove_quest", "locator": "Walkthrough: Wild/Vivid/Primal"}]

name: Lord's Trial
summary: Azmerian maze-festival to choose chieftains; raised Veruso to power and inspired Izaro's Labyrinth.

name: Maraketh Shrine
summary: Room-reward shrines in the PoE2 Trial of the Sekhemas. Each shrine (Tabina, Balbala, Ahkeli or Galai variants) lets the player spend 5 Sacred Water to restore part of their Honour, with a random Boon or Minor Affliction on some variants; the Fountain of Youth minor boon restores 40 Honour when a Maraketh Shrine is venerated.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_maraketh_shrine", "locator": "Full page (stub): 'Maraketh Shrines are found as room rewards in the Trial of the Sekhemas'; shrine list (Honour Tabina / Balbala / Ahkeli / Galai); Fountain of Youth minor boon"}]

name: Martyr of the First Edict (Void league leaderboard)
summary: Rise of the Abyssal mechanic: once per league a level-100 character can be sacrificed at the Site of the Chosen, sending it to the Void league and listing it as the 'Martyr of the First Edict' on the leaderboard. Meta/league flavour; no source explains the naming.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_rise_of_the_abyssal_league", "locator": "Site of the Chosen paragraph"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_league", "locator": "paragraph: 'listed as the Martyr of the First Edict on the leaderboard'"}]

name: Masters of the Atlas
summary: 0.5 storylines of three Atlas Masters: Jado (Order of the Djinn; unlocked by an anomaly map near the start), Hilda (monster hunter, Hilda's Campsite) and Doryani (unlocked by clearing a corruption nexus). The earlier draft's 'ascendancy-like specialisation' claim is unsupported and was removed.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_ggg_content_update_0_5_0", "locator": "Atlas Masters: Jado, Hilda, Doryani; Doryani questline via corruption nexus; Jado via anomaly map"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Atlas Masters"}, {"source_id": "src_web_pcgamesn_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Masters of the Atlas storyline"}]

name: Memory Tears and Threads
summary: Tears in Atlas reality where Zana's manifested memories leak; Eagon traces threads to Moments of Loneliness, Trauma, Reverence.

name: Nemesis modifier
summary: Nemesis modifiers were powerful extra modifiers on every rare monster in Nemesis league (hardcore); the league modifier was "Rare Monsters each have a Nemesis Mod".

name: The Pantheon
summary: Pantheon power system introduced by Sin after Tukohama's death: Sin captures the souls of the risen gods the exile kills in Part Two and lends the exile a small portion of their power. The Brine King, Arakaali, Solaris and Lunaris grant major god powers; Tukohama, Abberath, Ryslatha, Ralakesh, Gruthkul, Yugul, Garukhan and Shakari are minor gods.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_father_of_war", "locator": "After Tukohama: Sin introduces the Pantheon"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "'Sin is able to capture the souls of the Pantheon of gods'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_tsoagoth_the_brine_king", "locator": "Pantheon powers: major god power"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_garukhan_queen_of_the_winds", "locator": "Garukhan is a minor pantheon goddess"}]

name: Atlas of Worlds (PoE2)
summary: The PoE2 endgame map network, reached after the campaign via Doryani's Waygate and navigated with Waystones. Rebuilt in 0.5 (Return of the Ancients) with fixed points of interest, storylines and a fully unlockable Atlas passive tree.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest log: 'Use the Map Device and the Waystone to enter a Map'"}, {"source_id": "src_web_pcgamesn_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Atlas passive tree: Fully remade; zone quest chains"}]

name: Prophecy
summary: Prophecy system of Prophecy league (2.3.0); removed in 3.17.0; Pale Council bosses.

name: The Red Pyre
summary: Entity/title in Ailith's Word of the Dreamer ('The Red Pyre burns hot... The Dreamer once knew him, before his addiction'). The fire imagery and the book's subject (the four Breachlords that became Xesht) point to Xoph, Dark Embers; the identification is inferred, not stated.

name: Rite of the Nameless
summary: Ritual mechanic/quest stage: place the Head of the King on the Incomplete Effigy in Caer Tarth, use it to select five maps, complete Rituals there to collect effigy parts (Tangled Torso, Mossy Arm, Frayed Cloth, Brittle Arm, Ragged Cloth), activate the Effigy and perform the Rite to reach the Darkness and the Bodach. 0.5.5 campaign unique-boss Rituals work similarly.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_maji", "locator": "steps 24-54 (hidden comment block)"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_forbidden_rites", "locator": "unique boss Rituals work similarly to the Rite of the Nameless"}]

name: Ritual (altar mechanic)
summary: Ritual Altars spawn wave encounters inside a ritual circle; defeating monsters earns Favour/Tribute to buy items. PoE1 Ritual league gives no narrative; Vaal Ritual Altars may summon Atziri's Apparition; later Wildwood lore ties 'ritual altars' to the King in the Mists; PoE2 adopts it in Forbidden Rites.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_ritual_league", "locator": "lead paragraph and League mechanic"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_atziri_lore", "locator": "section 'Vaal Ritual Altar'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_forbidden_rites", "locator": "League content"}]

name: Ritual and the King in the Mists (PoE2)
summary: 0.5 Ritual storyline: Aoife, a lost spirit bound by the King in the Mists, appeals to the Wildwood; the prison beneath holds the Bodach; the Rite of the Nameless in Caer Tarth. 0.5.5 adds Ritual altars to every zone.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Ritual: Aoife, a lost spirit, bound by the King in the Mists... Bodach ... Rite of the Nameless"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_forbidden_rites", "locator": "League content"}]

name: Rogue exiles
summary: Exiled criminals who roam Wraeclast as hostile NPCs; originated in Anarchy league (0.11.0), later reused in PoE2 (Lichborn exiles in Rise of the Abyssal).

name: Rogue Exiles (PoE2)
summary: Roaming exile NPC bosses introduced in 0.2.0; Abyss can raise a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_dawn_of_the_hunt_league", "locator": "rogue exiles"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_rise_of_the_abyssal_league", "locator": "raising a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile"}]

name: Royal Order of Criminal Hanging
summary: A royal order to hang named criminals that was damaged by seawater on the voyage to Kingsmarch; Johan declined to enforce it because the reply would exceed the Charter's statute of limitations and he would not hang the wrong man.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_letter_kingsmarch_", "locator": "==Legal Response (Johan)==: \"the recent Royal Order of Criminal Hanging was damaged by seawater\"; \"the punishment in question will exceed the Charter statute of limitations\""}]

name: Sekhema
summary: Maraketh leader title; always a woman chosen by merit and anointed with the feather of the Great Roc; tale-women keep the people's history.

name: Shrine (Domination)
summary: Shrines are a mechanic introduced by Domination league (1.0.0); Domination's area modifier allowed shrines to spawn.

name: Strongbox
summary: Strongboxes are a mechanic introduced by Ambush league (1.1.0, March 2014); every area in Ambush carried the Ambush chests modifier.

name: Tempest
summary: Tempests are effects introduced by Tempest league that can change monster and player size, cause damage, alter drop rates, or animate weapons that drop; affected areas are shown on the World Screen.

name: Thaumaturgy
summary: Gem-based magic whose source is the Beast. Outlawed by Veruso, embraced by Chitus under Malachai's 'Thaumatocracy', and banned again by Voll.

name: The Decay
summary: Ancient cosmic mould-like entity ('the Oblivion') from outside time and space that turns all it touches to void; the Elder is its servant. Dormant after the Elder's defeat.

name: The Edicts (Precursor murals)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "Precursor age, far older than the Vaal and Winter of the World", "story_order": null}
summary: Series of vague Precursor murals described by the PoE2 wiki as depicting the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it; numbered First to Fourth in game. Known: Third = instrument is the Weapon (Hooded One recognises it as 'the Weapon I saw in that third mural'); Second = Doryani's guess that the Seed was its instrument; Fourth = investigated in the Epilogue after the Arbiter of Ash (PoE1 wiki editors speculate it caused the Great Fire); First = unexplained threat averted in the Epilogue. The full text of the edicts is not given in any source read. Not to be confused with Count Geonor's hanging edicts in Ogham.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "'It was depicted in their Edicts, vague murals that depicts the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'The Third Edict? What is the meaning... of these Edicts?'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural'; Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'"}]

name: The Pantheon (soul-capture mechanic)
summary: Game mechanic and lore device by which Sin captures the essences of slain gods and grants the Exile a fraction of their powers. Major gods: Brine King, Arakaali, Solaris, Lunaris. Minor gods: Tukohama, Abberath, Ryslatha (Act 6), Gruthkul, Ralakesh (Act 7), Yugul (Act 8), Garukhan, Shakari (Act 9).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "section 'The Pantheon'; Sin dialogue 'The Father of War': \"While a god may fall, their essence lingers... That essence can be yours\""}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "See also: The Pantheon"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_tsoagoth_the_brine_king", "locator": "Pantheon powers: major god power"}]

name: The Struggle
summary: Ancient conflict among cosmic forces (the Decay, the Tangle, the Cleansing Fire) introduced by the Envoy. The forces cannot clash directly without rending reality, so disputes are settled by duels between mortal champions. The Elder's defeat left a vacancy over the Atlas that drew the others in; the Maven, with the Exile as her champion and Kirac's Vanguard, stands against the Eldritch champions. A progenitor/Lightkeeper is cited as the order the forces are blind to.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_struggle", "locator": "lead + Order/Decay/Tangle/Cleansing Fire sections"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_decay", "locator": "lead: 'defeat of the Elder ... created a temporary vacancy'"}]

name: The Tangle
summary: Cosmic force served by the Infinite Hunger and the Eater of Worlds (flavour: sea of limbs, to eat, to feast).

name: Timeless Conflict
summary: Legions of different factions (Karui, Maraketh, Templar, Eternal Empire, Vaal) frozen in stasis by a timeless monolith, locked in an endless battle; broken out of stasis by damaging them. Why they are frozen is not explained in the wiki.

name: Tormented spirits
summary: Spirits of tormented criminals in Torment league (1.3.0) that flee, empower nearby monsters and drop loot; unrelated to Kitava's Torments in Act 5.

name: Trial of Chaos
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 3 at the Temple of Chaos via an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the quest item Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian). Based on the PoE1 Ultimatum league and overseen by the Trialmaster.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trial_of_chaos", "locator": "section 'Access'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_chaos_lore", "locator": "intro: 'The Trialmaster ... oversee the Trials of Chaos'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trial_of_chaos", "locator": "lead and Access"}]

name: Trial of the Sekhemas
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 2 via the Djinn Barya key (or the quest item Balbala's Barya), a gauntlet of up to 4 floors with bosses including Rattlecage, Hadi and Rafiq, Ashar and Zarokh.

name: Uber pinnacle bosses
summary: Harder repeatable versions: Uber Elder, Uber Sirus, Uber Maven, Uber Exarch/Eater after 24 influenced T14+ maps. Memory-version retellings per Day Zero.

name: Utopia (Twilight Order ideal)
summary: The Order's promised god-free world ('without gods... without suffering... without the disease of Divinity'), recruited for with 'Accept Utopia! Embrace the saviour!'. Art book: intention is good but its methods are contentious.

name: Vaal corruption and thaumaturgical technology
summary: Vaal science combined gem-craft, constructs, mechanical technology and corruption drawn from the Beast; much of it was developed by Doryani and housed at Atzoatl and Utzaal. Its influence resurfaces as Vaal side areas, Vaal skill gems and Vaal Orbs in PoE1.

name: Vaal sacrifice and Vaal souls
summary: Vaal bloodpriests discovered that the souls of the recently killed briefly seek another source of life and can be captured in a vaal skill gem to empower it; human and blood sacrifice powered Vaal constructs and society, and slavery supplied victims.

name: Verisium
summary: Metal ore found only in fallen meteorites and not native to Wraeclast; Kalguuran runes were typically crafted from it, and in PoE2 Act 4 Dannig forges Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots.

name: Virtue Gems
aliases: ["Tears of Maji", "Tears of the Maji", "Virtue gems"]
summary: Gems from the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy, buried by Veruso and mined by slaves under Chitus; infused into gemlings. Ubiquitous in Vaal society.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_azmeri", "locator": "Culture > Tears of Maji"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Tarcus Veruso'; 'Malachai'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'The Beast'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "History"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Vaal'"}]

name: Wildwood ascendancy classes
summary: Affliction's temporary ascendancies (Wildwood Primalist with charms, Warden of the Maji with tinctures, Warlock of the Mists with corpse items) earned through the Azmeri questlines; removed at league end.

name: Humours / Wisps (Wildwood)
summary: In the Viridian Wildwood the four humours (Primal, Vivid, Wild, Sacred) materialise as wisps. The first three share names with Harvest's Primal, Vivid and Wild Lifeforce colours. Sacred humours are harvested by the ritual altars of the King in the Mists.

name: Hiveborn
summary: Breach-spawn into which the Breachlords were evolving; the Keepers of the Flame, founded through Chayula's dreams, exist to destroy them. The Dreamer is revealed to be of the same kind as the Hiveborn.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_into_the_breach", "locator": "quest steps: Hiveborn invade Wraeclast"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_keepers_league", "locator": "League content"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Hiveborn"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_dreamer", "locator": "Lore: the Breachlords began their evolution into the Hiveborn; the Dreamer is the same creature as the Hiveborn"}]

name: Kitava's Heart
summary: A part of Kitava that spawns during its battle in Act 5 (Cathedral Rooftop, The Feeding Trough) and Act 10. Introduced as a boss monster in 3.0.0; since 3.2.0 it cannot be slowed below its base speed.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kitava_s_heart", "locator": "lead: 'Kitava's Heart is a part of Kitava that spawns during the battle with Kitava, the Insatiable, which occurs in Act 5 and Act 10'; Version history 3.0.0 'Introduced to the game as boss monster'; 3.2.0 speed note"}]

name: The Lightless (Abyssals)
summary: Ancient subterranean race created, not born, via necromancy, afraid of light; invaded during the Winter of the World and were driven back underground by the returning sun. Antagonists of Abyss and PoE2 Rise of the Abyssals.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lightless", "locator": "intro; Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Winter of the World > The Lightless"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lightless", "locator": "lead and Lore"}]

name: Metamorph
summary: Shape-shifting enemies assembled from organs of other monsters and bosses; they use the moves of whatever parts they carry.

name: Scourge monsters
summary: Blood-crazed demonic monsters of the Scourge Nightmare realm. After the league they became the core game's Beyond monsters, and currencies such as Tainted Blessing came from them.

name: Synthetes
summary: Synthesis league bosses (Altered, Augmented, Rewritten and Twisted Synthete) guarding fractured uniques; later unique-map bosses.

name: The Nameless
summary: Shadowy beings born with the Wildwood as the 'unseen reflection opposite the mortal world'; led by the King in the Mists; Gruthkul was one.

name: The Titans
summary: Primordial race that walked molten Wraeclast and inhabited its volcanoes; mostly indifferent to humans; nearly wiped out in the 'rising darkness', with the Molten One the sole survivor.

name: Trarthan mercenaries
summary: Lawless Trarthan veterans met in Mercenaries league; hirable allies with unique gear and skills; noble ones come from the four Great Houses.

name: The Undying
summary: Gemlings and citizens of Sarn transformed by the Cataclysm into mindless monsters that can live for centuries; some gemling legionnaires later regain sentience (Act 8 Grain Gate).

name: Vorniculia / horrors
summary: Horror species that attacked Kalguuran outposts; Olroth's Knights culled the Vorniculia.

name: Wisps (humours)
summary: Wildwood humours materialised as Primal, Vivid, Wild and Sacred wisps; freed wisps escape into the overworld empowering monsters; Sacred humours are harvested by the King in the Mists' ritual altars.

name: Abberath, the Cloven One
summary: Goatman god (the Cloven One, Quaffer of Souls) killed in the Valley of the Fire Drinker. Per Bestel, goatmen offer him humans and he eats them 'meat, soul and all'; per Sin he was once Abberath the Scholar King, an alchemist who burned flesh away to drink the life force within, starting with goats. Minor Pantheon god.

name: Arakaali, Spinner of Shadows
summary: Vaal spider-goddess of love and death, worshipped by Azmeri artists; consorts with Silk in the Temple of Decay and is killed as Act 7's boss. A relationship with Sin is hinted.

name: Arohongui, Daughter of the Moon
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. Daughter of Ramako's alleged impersonator and Sione; lacks the warmth and light of the Sun

name: The Beast
summary: Divine creature, source of thaumaturgy and corruption, grown by Sin from the Dark Ember beneath Highgate to keep the gods asleep. Has no will of its own; exploited by Doryani, Atziri, Chitus, Malachai. The Exile kills it in Act 4; PoE2 follows a new Beast grown from the stolen Seed of Corruption.

name: The Brine King
aliases: ["King of Brine", "Lord of Salt and Scale", "Old Briney", "Soygoth", "Tsoagoth", "Tsoagoth, the Brine King"]
summary: Azmeri king Tsoagoth turned god of storms and sea, worshipped by the Brinerot pirates with sacrifices; Act 6 Pantheon boss.

name: Chaos
aliases: ["Chaos (Impulse)", "Impulse of Chaos", "Lord Chaos", "Master of the Trialmaster"]
summary: Impulse able to see across timelines, once worshipped by Vaal priests; master of the Trialmaster and enemy-of-sorts to Hinekora's fixed prophecies.

name: Chayula, the Dreamer
summary: Breachlord known as the Dreamer or Benevolent Dreamer; PoE2 lore shows he aided the Third Pact alliance, was severed from the failed Breachlord merge, and formed the Keepers of the Flame through dreams. After Xesht falls Ailith reveals his ultimate aim is to subjugate all life as obedient thralls.

name: Craiceann, First of the Deep
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Deep ('First of All'), ancestor of crabs, squid and sea creatures; Bestiary encounter.

name: The Eater of Worlds
summary: Eldritch Horror serving the Tangle, fought in Absence of Symmetry and Harmony.

name: Esh, Forked Thought
summary: One of five Breachlords. Lightning damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Esh's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_esh_forked_thought", "locator": "lead + Version History"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_it_that_was_esh", "locator": "boss page: found in Hive Colony, encountered together with the other"}]

name: Farrul, First of the Plains
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Plains ('First of the Hunt'), ancestor of hounds, cats and other mammals; Bestiary encounter.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Ezomytes > The First Ones"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_first_ones", "locator": "section on Farrul"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_bestiary_league", "locator": "Spirit Beasts"}]

name: Fenumus, First of the Night
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Night ('First Explorer'), ancestor of bugs and insectoids; Bestiary encounter.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Ezomytes > The First Ones"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_first_ones", "locator": "section on Fenumus"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_bestiary_league", "locator": "Spirit Beasts"}]

name: Garukhan
aliases: ["Garukhan, Queen of the Winds", "Orbala", "Queen of the Winds"]
summary: Goddess of wind and sky, formerly the Maraketh Sekhema Orbala ('Sekhema of Sekhemas'); freed Sin from the cliff where Innocence's followers had chained him, became his lover and wife and bore Shakari; Sin planted the Dark Ember 'for Garukhan'.

name: The God of Domination
summary: Mysterious, possibly otherworldly god tied to the Harbingers; Harbinger uniques foretell its gaze falling over Wraeclast.

name: The Goddess of Justice
summary: Deity worshipped by Izaro Phrecius; known only by this title.

name: The Greatwolf
summary: First Ones-type god of the hunt and ancestor of wolves and werewolves; possessed Rigwald, the Wolven King, during the Purity Rebellion.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ezomytes", "locator": "The First Ones > The Greatwolf"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_first_ones", "locator": "The Greatwolf section"}]

name: Gruthkul
summary: Bestial minor god, Mother of Despair / Porcelain Queen, a mother whose children were slaughtered by Arakaali and whose grief made her a horned beast; Act 7 Pantheon boss. Sources disagree on the culprit: the God page says Arakaali slaughtered her children; Sin's dialogue says the Vaal laid waste to her kingdom; Sin's 'Mother of Despair' dialogue says her daughters plotted against Arakaali.

name: Halani
summary: Forgotten Maraketh water goddess, found powerless and dying from lack of worship in PoE2 Act 2 Buried Shrines; mother of Azarian.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_halani_the_water_goddess", "locator": "intro and dialogue with Azarian"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'Halani'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_city_of_seven_waters", "locator": "Walkthrough 'Talk to the Water Goddess' / 'End the Water Goddess' suffering'"}]

name: Hinekora
summary: Karui goddess, the Mother of Death, ruler of the Halls of the Dead, seer of prophecy; speaks through the Well of Passing and rewards the worthy with the Tattoo of Hinekora.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_hinekora", "locator": "section 'Lore'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_hinekora", "locator": "Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_trial_of_the_ancestors_quest", "locator": "Peer into the Well of Passing"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_hinekora", "locator": "dialogue quotes"}]

name: Innocence
summary: Templar god of light and purity, twin of Sin; per Lycia's relics his ascension was fuelled by turning followers against Sin. In Act 5 High Templar Avarius is his vessel; after Sin's 'more sensible host' (Bannon) sacrifices himself with the Staff of Purity in Act 10, he is reborn, helps defeat Kitava and then goes into self-exile in the far south.

name: Kamasa
summary: Vaal god of Wealth, represented by a monkey; in PoE2 Act 3 monkey-statue temples in Utzaal hold Kamasa treasure.

aliases: ["Father of Corruption", "Kitava, the Insatiable", "The Black Spirit", "The Cannibal King", "The Ravenous God", "The Ravenous One", "The Tormented One"]
summary: Karui god of chaos, hunger and corruption (Father of Corruption, the Cannibal King, Black Spirit); invited into Wraeclast by the Eternals per Karui lore, devours Oriath and is slain by the Exile with Sin and Innocence in Act 10.

name: Kopec
summary: Vaal sun god; the Temple of Kopec in Utzaal sealed the time gateway.

name: Kulemak
summary: Master of the Lightless and creator of the Lich Lords; exalted within the Well of Souls (which arose after The Master Below All 'raged'), he waged the Winter of the World against the surface until the Three Sisters destroyed his mortal form; his soul returned to the Well. Namesake of the Horns of Kulemak (Immortal Syndicate). PoE2 pinnacle of the Well of Souls content.

summary: Karui Mother of the Moon (the Karui sister name for the lunar goddess), involved in the myth of Ramako and Arohongui. Note: The Three Sisters page lists Lani Lua as sun and Sione as moon, contradicting the God page (Lani Lua moon, Sione sun); the wiki is inconsistent.

name: The Lightkeeper (the Progenitor)
summary: Progenitor figure named by the Envoy: the Cleansing Fire is blind to 'the path set before it by the lightkeeper'; Struggle page says he tests the limits of limitless power and directs the weavers of destiny. Nature and relation to the Maven unresolved.

name: Lunaris
summary: Eternal/Azmeri moon goddess, sister of Solaris; her rivalry was engineered by Tangmazu. (PoE2 appearance of Solaris/Lunaris by name not verified in the local PoE2 corpus; Maraketh variants Solerai/Lundara and the Three Sisters myth cover PoE2.)

name: The Master Below All
summary: Ancient being whose rage created the Well of Souls, power source of necromancy; nothing else known.

name: Ngamahu
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "section 'Ngamahu'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_ngamahu_s_test", "locator": "Halls of the Dead test; Karui tattoos by god's domain"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui", "locator": "tribe list"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Arohongui/Ramako/Rongokurai paragraph (Karui myth)"}]

name: Order
summary: Impulse opposed to Chaos, representing dominion and control; Hinekora is its servant per wiki analysis; in one timeline Order overcame Chaos through Venarius's enslavement of humanity.

name: Prospero
summary: Azmerian god of wealth and the underworld, patron of the Perandus family; Cadiro struck a deal for long life.

name: Ralakesh
aliases: ["Master of a Million Faces", "Ralakesh, Master of a Million Faces"]
summary: God of subjugation and control, Master of a Million Faces, brother of Tangmazu. Eramir says he ruled a Vaal city and enslaved Azmeri to repopulate it; the God page lists him among Azmerian/Eternal gods. His relic possessed Greust; in the Act 7 quest The Master of a Million Faces the Exile kills Greust and Sin then drains and kills Ralakesh.

summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. claimed he was impersonated

name: Rongokurai, Father of the Night
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. whose darkness covered the visits to Sione

name: Ryslatha, the Puppet Mistress
summary: Parasite-queen goddess (a carrion-insect queen covered in parasites) found in the Spawning Ground of the Wetlands. Per Sin she was once a revered matriarch whose children were slaughtered by Tukohama's warriors and who now wants to make everyone's children hers; the Azmeri believed her offspring would one day overwhelm the world. Minor Pantheon god.

name: Saqawal, First of the Sky
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Sky ('Last of the First'), ancestor of birds and reptiles; Bestiary encounter.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Ezomytes > The First Ones"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_first_ones", "locator": "section on Saqawal"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_bestiary_league", "locator": "Spirit Beasts"}]

name: The Searing Exarch
summary: Eldritch Horror serving the Cleansing Fire; seeks to master the Atlas; fought in the Absence of Patience and Wisdom.

name: Shakari, Queen of the Sands
summary: Maraketh scorpion-goddess, daughter of Sin and Garukhan; hides in the Oasis behind a sandstorm rebuilding an ancient army and is killed in the Sand Pit (Act 9). Minor Pantheon god.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_shakari_queen_of_the_sands", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'Shakari'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_shakari_queen_of_the_sands", "locator": "Intro: daughter of Garukhan and Sin"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_queen_of_the_sands", "locator": "Sin: 'corrupted daughter'"}]

name: Sin
aliases: ["Original Evil", "Sin, the Thief of Virtue", "The Forgotten One", "The Hooded One", "The Hooded One (PoE2)", "Thief of Virtue"]
summary: God, brother (twin, per the stained-glass windows) of Innocence; planted the Dark Ember beneath Highgate from which the Beast grew. In PoE1 he guides the Exile against Kitava; in PoE2 the Hooded One reveals in Act 2 that he is Sin.

name: Sione
summary: Karui Mother of the Sun, wife of Ramako, locked in endless battle with Lani Lua. See Lani Lua node for wiki inconsistency on which is sun/moon.

name: Solaris
summary: Eternal/Azmeri sun goddess, twin sister of Lunaris; led a rival cult after Tangmazu tricked her into believing Lunaris betrayed her. Sin has her soul captured for the Pantheon in Act 8. (PoE2 appearance of Solaris/Lunaris by name not verified in the local PoE2 corpus; Maraketh variants Solerai/Lundara and the Three Sisters myth cover PoE2.)
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'Solaris and Lunaris'"}, {"source_id": "src_ingame_sin_dialogue", "locator": "Sin 'Solaris' dialogue"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_three_sisters", "locator": "Eternals: Solaris (sun), Lunaris (moon)"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_solaris_eternal_sun", "locator": "Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_solaris_and_lunaris", "locator": "Final bosses of Act 8"}]

name: Tangmazu
aliases: ["Black Crow", "Raven Trickster", "Strange Voice", "Tangmazu, the Trickster God (Freya Hartlin)", "Tekaru", "Tekaru the Deceiver", "The Trickster"]
summary: Trickster god (Tekaru to the Karui, Black Crow to the Ezomytes), Ralakesh's brother, said to have made Solaris and Lunaris fight; listed on the wiki as an NPC related to Delirium and, in PoE2, revealed as the disguised Freya Hartlin whose release triggers a Delirium encounter.

name: Tasalio
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "section 'Tasalio'; Haku level 7 dialogue"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui", "locator": "tribe list"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Arohongui/Ramako/Rongokurai paragraph (Karui myth)"}]

name: Tawhoa
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.

name: The Bodach
summary: Dark entity fought as the final boss of Legacy of the Maji after the Rite of the Nameless ('Explore the Darkness'; 'Defeat the Bodach'); the official 0.5.0 text says a prison beneath Caer Tarth holds it. At T14+ it is the Ritual pinnacle per a guide.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_three_sisters", "locator": "paragraph 3: Sisters sealed away the Bodach"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_bodach", "locator": "intro and Phase 1b"}, {"source_id": "src_other_timesaver_bodach", "locator": "Rite of the Nameless summary (third-party)"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_maji", "locator": "steps 53-54 'Explore the Darkness', 'Defeat the Bodach'; completion: Defeat The Bodach"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "The prison beneath it holds the Bodach"}, {"source_id": "src_web_timesaver_pinnacle_bosses", "locator": "Bodach appears at Tier 14+"}]

name: The Draiocht
summary: Goddess protecting the Azmeri, divided into the Three Sisters Mhacha, Catha, Morrigan who gave themselves to imbue nature; created the Wildwood and forbade gems. Original name lost.

name: The First Ones
summary: Animalistic gods worshipped by the Ezomytes, believed to roam the realm of Spirit; their avatars are Spirit Beasts: Saqawal (birds/reptiles, 'Last of the First'), Farrul (hounds/cats/mammals, 'First of the Hunt'), Fenumus (insects, 'First Explorer'), Craiceann (crabs/squid/sea life, 'First of All'). Also The Greatwolf and the Gull.

name: The Forgotten Daughter
summary: Unique monster in Act 2 Fellshrine Ruins representing Sin and Innocence's sister, from before the gods; presumably never ascended.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'The Forgotten Daughter'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "sister, 'whom he only vaguely recalls'"}]

name: The Molten One
summary: Last surviving Titan from a prehistoric era, worshipped indirectly as the volcano home of the Redblade warband; writes environmental lore found in the Forge of the Titans.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_molten_one", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "section 'The Molten One'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "line 188 'The last known remaining Titan'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Titans/rising darkness paragraph"}]

name: The Spirit
summary: Mysterious entity with which Yeena (Act 2) communicates; listed among Azmerian/Eternal gods on the God page. Nothing more is stated.

name: Thruldana
summary: God whose name Undertaker Arimor invokes in a chant; nothing else is known.

name: Tukohama
aliases: ["Father of War", "Tukohama, Karui God of War"]
summary: Karui god of war; his tooth slashed Kitava's face. Revived by the Beast's death, he raises the Karui Fortress and is the first god the Exile captures for the Pantheon in Act 6. Kaom claimed to be his son (carvings in Kaom's Stronghold).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "section 'Tukohama'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_tukohama_karui_god_of_war", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_tukohama_karui_god_of_war", "locator": "Act 6 boss; first Pantheon power"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_father_of_war", "locator": "Walkthrough"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Tavakai phase 2/3 dialogue"}]

name: Tul, Creeping Avalanche
summary: One of five Breachlords. Cold Breachlord (female per wiki). Boss residing in Tul's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_tul_creeping_avalanche", "locator": "lead + Version History"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_it_that_was_tul", "locator": "boss page: found in Hive Colony, encountered together with the other"}]

name: Uul-Netol, Unburdened Flesh
summary: One of five Breachlords. Physical damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Uul-Netol's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

name: Vaal Oversoul
summary: Shadowy Vaal spirit entity at the top of the Ancient Pyramid; final boss of Act 2; summoned by The Apex on the Dark Altar.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_vaal_oversoul", "locator": "intro; map variant 'Vessel of the Vaal'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_vaal_oversoul", "locator": "boss header; Shadow of the Vaal"}, {"source_id": "src_ingame_vaal_oversoul", "locator": "boss header; Shadow of the Vaal"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_vaal_oversoul", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_doryani", "locator": "section 'Atziri's rule', Doryani's Machinarium flavour text"}]

name: Valako
summary: Karui god of storms and lightning; his jaw became a fish hook, one of Kitava's Torments.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_karui_gods", "locator": "section 'Valako'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kitava_s_torments", "locator": "Lani: 'A fish hook that was once the Valako's Jaw'"}]

name: Viridi
summary: Third sister of Solaris and Lunaris, Azmeri goddess of the earth, trapped within 'the orb' in Azmeri creation myth; probable namesake of the Viridian Wildwood.

name: Xesht
aliases: ["Xesht", "Xesht, We That Are One", "Xesht, We Who Are One", "Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand"]
summary: Incomplete union of the Breachlords Xoph, Tul, Esh and Uul-Netol after the five-Breachlord merge failed (Chayula was severed); filled with mindless rage and hunger. PoE1 fought it as Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand; in PoE2 0.5 it is the Breach pinnacle ('Xesht, We That Are One' per a guide), reached through a Breachstone/Realmgate.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_xesht-ula_the_open_hand", "locator": "Trivia: Xesht is the incomplete fusion of Xoph, Esh, Tul, Uul-Netol; Chayula opposes as the Dreamer"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_dreamer_npc_", "locator": "Dialogue \"Who is our enemy?\": \"Xoph... Esh... Tul... Uul-Netol... our melding... failed... They became Xesht.\""}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_dreamer", "locator": "Lore: failed merge of the five Breachlords; Chayula severed, rest formed Xesht"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_dreamer", "locator": "Lore: failed merge; the rest of the Breachlords formed an incomplete union in the form of Xesht"}, {"source_id": "src_web_domistae_poe2_endgame_guide", "locator": "Xesht: fought by communing with the Dreamer"}, {"source_id": "src_web_timesaver_pinnacle_bosses", "locator": "Xesht, We That Are One: Breach Splinters form a Breachstone, slotted into the Realmgate"}]

name: Xoph, Dark Embers
summary: One of five Breachlords (fire). Boss of Xoph's Domain, accessed via Xoph's Breachstone in a map device (2.5.0; removed from game 3.28.0). Model based on a Marauder; one of four lords fused into Xesht.

name: Yaomac
summary: Ancient Vaal god with three serpentine heads, worshipped by Vaalish priests. Ixchel stole his sleeping body for the Order of the Djinn; the Trialmaster refers to Yaomac when the player wins five or more times.

name: Yugul, Reflection of Terror
summary: Former Vaal scholar of fear who ascended by terrifying children and Vaal leaders; a maw-god killed in the High Gardens.

name: Ancient Azmeri/Ezomyte Age
aliases: ["Ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui Era"]
summary: Era of the primeval civilisation, Winter of the World, Lightless war and the ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui peoples, before the Eternal Empire (1 IC).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "sections Primeval civilization, The Azmeri, The Maraketh, The Ezomytes"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro paragraph 2; sections 'The Azmeri', 'The Ezomytes', 'The Karui'"}]

name: Eternal Empire (era)
summary: Umbrella period of the Eternal Empire (Sarn Empire) from Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC) through the Reign of Voll to the Cataclysm (~1339 IC). Split into the era_eternal_empire_rise and era_eternal_empire_fall buckets; the faction itself is faction_eternal_empire.

name: Eternal Empire Fall
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "c. 334 IC to c. 1339 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: The later Eternal Empire: Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth (1317 IC), Chitus and the gemling legions, the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) and the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) that ends the empire. Boundary with the 'rise' bucket is a convention.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "sections 'Reign of Izaro', 'The Purity Rebellion', 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'"}]

name: Eternal Empire Rise
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "1 IC to c. 334 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: From 1 IC: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn and the Eternal Empire; the empire expands; the Night of a Thousand Ribbons (c. 334 IC) ends Romira's reign.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Eternal Empire': 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)', 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'"}]

name: Interlude Between Games
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "about 20 years after Kitava's defeat", "story_order": null}
summary: About 20 years between the defeat of Kitava and the PoE2 prelude: Count Geonor, Ogham, and the release of the Seed of Corruption.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_lore", "locator": "section 'Prelude / Count Geonor' ('twenty years after the defeat of Kitava')"}]

name: PoE1 (era umbrella)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "before the ~20-year interlude that precedes PoE2", "story_order": null}
summary: Umbrella for the PoE1-era buckets: the Acts 1-10 campaign and Epilogue (era_poe1_campaign), the Atlas storylines (era_poe1_atlas) and league stories (era_poe1_leagues). Meta grouping only; no in-world event.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 3: 'An exile was responsible for killing the Beast around 20 years prior to the events of Path of Exile 2', which places the PoE1 events before the PoE2 era"}]

name: PoE1 Atlas Storylines
summary: Endgame Atlas storylines after the campaign: the Shaper and the Elder, and later the Conquerors of the Atlas. Dates are not given beyond the 'Day Zero' rule.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Atlas of Worlds' and 'The Elder and the Shaper'"}]

name: PoE1 Campaign (Acts 1-10)
summary: The Exile's first story: sentenced to Wraeclast by High Templar Dominus in 1599-1600 IC, the Exile crosses Wraeclast, defeats Dominus, and ends by defeating Kitava in Act 10.

name: PoE1 League Stories
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "run alongside PoE1 (no fixed date)", "story_order": null}
summary: League-specific storylines that the wiki's 'Day Zero' rule places alongside PoE1; the Exile wakes up in the sand of the Twilight Strand each league.

name: PoE2 (era umbrella)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "c. 20 years after the Beast's death", "story_order": null}
summary: Umbrella for the PoE2-era buckets: the Acts 1-6 campaign and interludes (era_poe2_campaign) and endgame and league storylines (era_poe2_endgame). Begins after the ~20-year interlude following the PoE1 kill of the Beast. Meta grouping only.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_beast", "locator": "paragraph 3: 'An exile was responsible for killing the Beast around 20 years prior to the events of Path of Exile 2'"}]

name: PoE2 Campaign
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "PoE2 campaign, after the interlude", "story_order": null}
summary: The PoE2 campaign: the Exile chases the Seed of Corruption across Wraeclast, starting in Ogham (Act 1).

name: PoE2 Endgame
summary: PoE2 endgame storylines after the campaign. Not covered in detail in this domain.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_lore", "locator": "section 'Notes' (endgame sections not covered by this domain)"}]

name: Post-Cataclysm Oriath
summary: Oriath, the island unaffected by the Cataclysm, becomes a Templar theocracy; the Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius. Roughly 260 years pass before PoE1.

name: Post-Vaal Dark Age
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "between the Vaal Cataclysm and 1 IC", "story_order": null}
summary: Ruins of the Vaal, the surviving Vaal absorbed into the Azmeri, and the Kalguur expedition that colonised and failed on Wraeclast.

name: Precursor Era
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "before the Winter of the World", "story_order": null}
summary: Age of the Precursor civilisation, the only culture wholly predating the Winter of the World; its apex lies further before the Vaal than the Vaal lie before the present.

name: Primordial Wraeclast
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "before the Vaal; earliest prehistory (exact years unknown)", "story_order": null}
summary: Earliest prehistory: a molten world with Kalandra trapped in her lake, the Titans, the Winter of the World and the Lightless attack. The wiki says the order of prehistoric events is unclear.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory: 'When Wraeclast was a primordial molten world of ooze and magma'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'Prehistory' and intro paragraphs 1-2"}]

name: Vaal Era
summary: The Vaal Empire under Queen Atziri, the use of virtue gems and sacrifice, ending in the Vaal Cataclysm.

name: A Dirty Job
summary: Tarkleigh sends the Exile to clear the Fetid Pool of the necromancer Kadavrus the Defiler who raises the dead rhoa. (Optional quest.)

name: Breaking Down the Door
summary: Act 1 quest exclusive to the Betrayal league (historical). Jun asks the Exile to help dismantle Immortal Syndicate fortifications on the Coast and to defeat a Syndicate member there. It was replaced by The Immortal Syndicate after the league ended.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_breaking_down_the_door", "locator": "Header: 'was a quest in Act 1 exclusive to the Betrayal league. After the league end it is replaced by The Immortal Syndicate'; Walkthrough: 'Jun wants you to help her find and dismantle the Immortal Syndicate fortifications on the Coast'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_breaking_down_the_door", "locator": "lead: 'was a quest in Act 1 exclusive to the Betrayal league. After the league end it is replaced by The Immortal Syndicate'; walkthrough: 'Jun wants you to help her find and dismantle the Immortal Syndicate fortifications on the Coast'"}]

name: Breaking Some Eggs
summary: The Exile finds three Karui glyph shells in rhoa nests and fits them to the glyph wall in the Mud Flats to drain the Submerged Passage.

name: The Caged Brute
summary: The Exile kills Brutus, Warden of Axiom Prison, in the Warden's Chambers, opening the way through the Prison.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_caged_brute", "locator": "Walkthrough; Nessa dialogue on Brutus myth"}, {"source_id": "src_ingame_the_caged_brute", "locator": "Walkthrough; Nessa dialogue on Brutus myth"}]

name: The Dweller of the Deep
summary: Tarkleigh asks the Exile to kill a giant crab nesting in the Flooded Depths. (Optional quest.)

name: Dying for a Fight
summary: Optional tutorial quest for the Trial of the Ancestors (Ancestor league, historical). A Silver Coin opens a portal to the Halls of the Dead; Navali, a revenant, tells the Exile that they have apparently died and sends them into the Halls of the Dead, where winning a tournament completes the quest.
