summary: Challenge league in which a Ritual Altar in each zone starts a wave fight that awards Tribute, spendable on a shop of pre-identified items. Narrative content is minimal in PoE1; the same Ritual altar mechanic returns in PoE2's Forbidden Rites league (0.5.5).

name: Sacrifice of the Vaal
summary: PoE1 1.1.0 mini-expansion centred on Atziri and Vaal side areas.

name: Sanctum league (The Forbidden Sanctum)
summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.20.0 (9 Dec 2022 - 4 Apr 2023; shipped as 'Path of Exile: The Forbidden Sanctum'): a roguelite run through an ancient Templar enclave beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, controlled by a malevolent entity (Lycia is its fourth-floor boss).

name: Scourge league
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "3.16.0 'Path of Exile: Scourge', 2021-10-22 to 2022-02-01", "story_order": null}
summary: Challenge league in which The Last to Die gives the exile a Blood Crucible to corrupt items while fighting through a demon-ridden 'Nightmare' mirror of Wraeclast; its monsters became the new Beyond monsters.

name: Path of Exile: Secrets of the Atlas
summary: PoE1 expansion 3.26.0 (13 Jun 2025) containing Mercenaries league and the Originator endgame storyline (Zana the Originator, Eagon Caeserius, Threads of the Originator); Settlers' Kingsmarch services were added to the core game.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_mercenaries_league", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_threads_of_the_originator", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_exploring_kingsmarch", "locator": "Version history 3.26.0"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_threads_of_the_originator", "locator": "Version history 3.26.0 / 3.28.0"}, {"source_id": "src_ggg_secrets_of_the_atlas_forum", "locator": "announcement"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_mercenaries_league", "locator": "release 2025-06-13, 'Path of Exile: Secrets of the Atlas' 3.26.0"}]

name: Sentinel league
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "3.18.0 'Path of Exile: Sentinel', 2022-05-13 to 2022-08-16", "story_order": null}
summary: Challenge league in which Sentinel drones empower monsters; Power Cores charge Sentinel filaments and Recombinators combine two equipment items. Sentinel mechanics were added to the core game in 3.25; existing Recombinators remained usable.

name: Settlers of Kalguur league
summary: PoE1 expansion/league 3.25.0 (26 Jul 2024; league ended 9 Jun 2025 22:00 UTC / 10 Jun 2025 00:00 GMT+2 per GGG after multiple extensions for PoE2 Early Access, over 45 weeks): the Exile helps Kalguuran settlers build Kingsmarch, a harbour meant to facilitate trade between the settlers, the Karui archipelago and Kalguur. Town-building ended in 3.26.0; Kingsmarch services joined the core game.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_settlers_league", "locator": "intro + '==League mechanic=='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_path_of_exile_settlers_of_kalguur", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_ggg_settlers_end", "locator": "GGG forum \"What Will Happen When The Settlers League Ends\": \"The league will end on Jun 10, 2025 12:00 AM (GMT+2)\"; \"Kingsmarch will be going core in 3.26\""}]

name: Siege of the Atlas (3.17.0)
summary: Expansion that added the Searing Exarch, Eater of Worlds and the Eldritch system.

name: Synthesis league
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "3.6.0 'Path of Exile: Synthesis', 2019-03-08 to 2019-06-03", "story_order": null}
summary: Challenge league in which fragments of lost memories are scattered through Wraeclast; the player stabilises them and links them in the Memory Nexus. Guide NPC Cavas turns out to be the High Templar Venarius. Not added to the core game; its bosses (Synthetes, Venarius) survive as unique maps.

name: Talisman league
summary: Talisman league launched 2015-12-11 (version 2.1.0). Monsters are possessed by ancient Ezomyte Talismans; killing them yields the Talisman. Boss: Rigwald, the Wolven King.

name: Tempest league
summary: Tempest league launched 2015-07-10 (2.0.0, The Awakening); hardcore sibling of Warbands that introduced Tempests, area modifiers that alter monsters and players (size, damage, drops).

name: Torment league
summary: Torment league launched 2014-12-13 (1.3.0): spirits of tormented criminals haunt areas, flee when met, imbue monsters and yield their ill-gotten gains when slain. Hardcore twin: Bloodlines.

name: Ultimatum league
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "3.14.0 'Path of Exile: Ultimatum', 2021-04-16 to 2021-07-19", "story_order": null}
summary: Vaal-themed challenge league in which the Trialmaster, servant of the entity Chaos, offers escalating Trials of Chaos for the player to risk or bank rewards. Re-integrated into the core game in 3.23.0.

name: Warbands league
summary: Warbands league Launched 2015-07-10 (version 2.0.0). Warring clans (Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind) roam Wraeclast in synergistic groups with leaders and elites. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

name: Abandoned Prison / Solitary Confinement
summary: Eternal Empire prison island; staff fed prisoners their own regrowing flesh after the Cataclysm (Tattered Diary). Solitary Confinement holds The Prisoner, sealed by Emperor Chitus under an order from Izaro.

name: Absence of Mercy and Empathy
summary: The Maven's realm in the Atlas; entering it with a The Maven's Writ starts The Maven's Game epilogue quest and hosts the Maven pinnacle fight.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_maven_s_game", "locator": "intro paragraph: 'This quest will automatically be obtained after entering Absence of Mercy and Empathy using a The Maven's Writ'"}]

name: Absence of Patience and Wisdom
summary: Atlas map realm where The Searing Exarch is fought in the Searing Exarch epilogue quest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_searing_exarch_quest", "locator": "Quest log: 'Enter The Absence of Patience and Wisdom'"}]

name: Absence of Symmetry and Harmony
summary: Atlas map realm where The Eater of Worlds is fought in the Eater of Worlds epilogue quest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_eater_of_worlds_quest", "locator": "Quest log: 'Enter Absence of Symmetry and Harmony'"}]

name: Absence of Value and Meaning
summary: Elder's arena in the Atlas.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_elder_quest", "locator": "'defeat The Elder in Absence of Value and Meaning'"}]

name: Abyssal Depths
summary: Areas reached from Abysses containing Abyssal monsters and lich bosses Amanamu and Ulaman.

name: Abyssal Depths (Delve)
summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) that uses Abyss theme and contains Abyss monsters. It is distinct from the Abyssal City biome (which spawns The Lich's Tomb) and from the Abyssal Depths map area (existing node loc_abyssal_depths).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_abyssal_depths_delve", "locator": "Intro: 'Abyssal Depths is a biome within the Azurite Mine'; hatnote: 'For the area accessible from completing an Abyss encounter in map'; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game.'"}]

name: Aggorat
summary: Opulent Vaal district of Utzaal, known for golden tributes at its main temple's apex; in the past it holds the Black Chambers where Doryani keeps Alva. In the present the Exile reaches it via the Drowned City and the Apex of Filth, defeating the Queen of Filth for the Temple Door Idol.

name: The Alluring Abyss
summary: PoE1 area for Uber Atziri (Mortal fragments).

name: Ancient Gateway
summary: Precursor gateway site the Exile reaches in Legacy of the Precursors after the Precursor Fortress rises; the Exile uses its levers and a Precursor Beacon there to open the route to the Burning Monolith.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest log: 'Travel to the Ancient Gateway', 'Explore the Ancient Gateway', 'Find and use Levers', 'Activate the Precursor Beacon'"}]

name: The Ancient Pyramid (PoE1 Act 2)
summary: Vaal pyramid in Act 2 housing the Dark Altar where the Vaal Oversoul is fought.

name: The Apex of Sacrifice
summary: PoE1 map-device area (Sacrifice fragments) in which Atziri is fought.

name: Arastas
summary: Karui-archipelago island in Act 4 where the Twilight Order's church and Torvian are found; the Excavation lies beyond.

name: The Ardura Caravan
summary: Mobile Maraketh caravan and Act 2 town hub, led by Zarka and Sekhema Asala.

name: Atlas of Worlds
summary: The dreamlike plane of interlinked worlds at the centre of PoE1's endgame; its mists reflect the desires of whoever walks it (Veritania's journal). Time there is 'a mirage' (Baran). Reached via the Map Device.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_veritania_s_journals", "locator": "Journal I: 'There is only my will, my thoughts, and my expectations, reflected as countless echoes'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_baran_s_journals", "locator": "Journal III: 'Time in the Atlas is a mirage'"}]

name: Atziri's Temple (Lira Vaal)
summary: Past version of the temple unlocked via Ancient Beacons; the present ruin is the Lost Temple. Built via the Temple Console; Doryani turns the entrance into a time portal after Act 3/4.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_atziri_s_temple", "locator": "lead; Ancient Beacon; Doryani will activate the time portal"}]

name: Aul's Domain (Crystal King's Throne)
summary: Delve area (internally 'Proto-Vaal city') of the Azurite Mine where the crystal-encased citadel and throne of Aul, the Crystal King, lie.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Primeval civilization; footnote: 'Proto-Vaal' is the internal name of Delve's Primeval Chamber and The Crystal King's Throne"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_aul_the_crystal_king", "locator": "lead"}]

name: Axiom Prison
summary: Ancient clifftop prison (no one remembers who built it) used by every power that ruled Wraeclast; its warden Brutus was mutated; Act 1 area from Lower Prison to Warden's Chambers.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Axiom Prison'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_brutus_lord_incarcerator", "locator": "Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_essence_of_umbra", "locator": "Shavronne in her tower in the Prison"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_father_of_war", "locator": "Tarkleigh on reaching Axiom Prison"}]

name: The Azak Bog
summary: Act 3 swamp area where the Azak tribe lives; site of Ignagduk's arena at Gor-gor Mog and the start of the Tribal Vengeance quest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tribal_vengeance", "locator": "Lead: 'a quest in the act 3 area The Azak Bog'; 'Start' field"}]

name: Azala Vaal
summary: Vaal capital named after the burning of Lira Vaal's temple; now buried beneath Sarn where the Azmeri founded the Eternal Empire's capital.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'The Capital'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Tarcus Veruso: 'ruins of Azala Vaal'"}]

name: Viridian Wildwood
summary: Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons there, the Maji fight the Nameless and the King in the Mists. PoE2 Last of the Druids setting.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Winter of the World > The Viridian Wildwood"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_azmeri", "locator": "Culture > The Maji"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'===The Viridian Wildwood===' lines 147-153"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Viridian Wildwood'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_chaos_lore", "locator": "paragraph on the forest not existing until 3.23.0"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_forbidden_rites", "locator": "Viridian Wildwood encounter"}, {"source_id": "src_web_gamedeveloper_return_of_the_ancients", "locator": "Wildwood"}]

name: Azmerian Ranges
summary: Mountain homeland of the ancient Azmeri; origin of the migrants who founded Sarn and the Eternal Empire, and where the Vaal first met the Azmeri.

name: The Azurite Mine
summary: Infinitely scaling dungeon beneath Wraeclast reached from the Mine Encampment; contains Primeval ruins, Vaal city, abyssal city biomes and darkness.

name: The Belly of the Beast
summary: Interior of the Beast with the Black Core.

name: The Black Chambers
summary: Complex within Aggorat where Doryani keeps Alva in the past of Utzaal; Act 3 boss area where the Exile captures Doryani (act boss: Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest log 'Find Doryani in the Black Chambers'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_3", "locator": "Progression table"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "quest log"}]

name: The Bone Pits
summary: Site in the Mastodon Badlands where Ekbab and Iktab guard the Mastodon Tusks.

name: The Brine King's Reef
summary: Blood-reef boss area at the end of Act 6, reached by Weylam Roth's ship the Black Crest, summoned with the Black Flag at the Beacon.

name: Buried Shrines
summary: Shrine area of Keth guarded by Azarian, the Forsaken Son.

name: Caer Tarth
summary: Ritual hub on the 0.5 Atlas, west of the starting point.

name: The Cathedral Rooftop (Act 10)
summary: Rooftop where Bannon holds off Kitava's cultists.

name: Cemetery of the Eternals
summary: PoE2 Act 1 area in Ogham where Eternal praetors are entombed, with inscriptions claiming the land 'in life and death'.

name: Chamber of Innocence
summary: Templar chamber in Oriath built under High Templar Avarius whose stained glass windows tell the Sin and Innocence story.

name: Chamber of Sins
summary: Laboratory built by Chitus where Maligaro conducted flesh experiments, opposed by nearby Phrecia Cathedral; named by Archbishop Geofri.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Maligaro'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_intruders_in_black", "locator": "Walkthrough"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_master_of_a_million_faces", "locator": "Helena on the secret passage"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_maligaro", "locator": "Chamber of Sins"}]

name: Chimeral Wetlands
summary: Wetland crossed on the way to Jiquani's Machinarium, guarded by Xyclucian.

name: Clearfell
summary: Ezomyte logging encampment in Ogham that serves as Act 1's town hub, where Una and Renly operate.

name: The Control Blocks
summary: Templar prison blocks in Oriath.

name: Crux of Nothingness
summary: Atlas site revealed with An Audience with the King where the King in the Mists is fought in the Ritual quest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_maji", "locator": "steps 14-17 'Reveal the Crux of Nothingness ... Defeat the King in the Mists'"}]

name: The Crystal Veins
summary: Highgate caverns holding the Rapture Device, which the exile reactivates to enter the Beast.

name: Cuachic Vault
summary: Isolated vault atop Mount Kriar where a Vaal remnant (Cuachic) lived, controlled and numbed by their High Priests.

name: Mines (Delve)
summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) that generates only at the top levels of the mine; contains Metallic, Serrated, Pristine and Aetheric fossils. Introduced in 3.4.0.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_mines_delve", "locator": "Intro: 'Mines is one of the biomes of the Azurite Mine. It only generates at the very top levels of the mine'; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game'"}]

name: Deshar
summary: Maraketh burial site with the Burial Spires, where the honoured dead are given sky burials.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest log 'Use the Desert Map to travel to Deshar'"}]

name: Doedre's Cesspool
summary: Sewer area of the Toxic Conduits in Sarn where Doedre is killed in the Cauldron.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_essence_of_the_hag", "locator": "Doedre's Cesspool contains The Cauldron boss arena"}]

name: Domain of Timeless Conflict
summary: Area opened by combining Emblems in the map device; heart of the timeless conflict between legions.

name: The Drowned City
summary: Submerged city section revealed after the lake is drained.

name: The Ebony Barracks
summary: Blackguard base across the river in Sarn.

name: Western and Eastern Enigma Chambers
summary: Two endgame chambers entered through the Western and Eastern Gateways; each holds a boss fight (Count Geonor in the west, Doryani in the east) and a Crisis Fragment (Ancient and Weathered) needed to open the Burning Monolith.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest log (hidden comment block): 'Travel to the Western Enigma Chamber', 'Defeat Count Geonor', 'Defeat Doryani', 'Pick up the Ancient Crisis Fragment'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_burning_monolith", "locator": "Keys: 'The other two keys can be found in the Western Enigma Chamber and the Eastern Enigma Chamber.'"}]

name: Eternal Laboratory
summary: Malachai's laboratory of the Eternal Empire, built on the archbishop Lazhwar's thaumaturgy research into maps; Zana's hideout alternative in the legacy Atlas quests.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Eternal Empire section: 'Lazhwar... discovered maps to create the Eternal Laboratory'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_shaper_quest", "locator": "Assignment: 'Talk to Zana in your Hideout or the Eternal Laboratory'"}]

name: Eye of Hinekora / Halls of the Dead
summary: Karui afterlife realm unlocked by rescuing Matiki: Tests of Mettle for Kaom, Maata and Rakiata, the Halls of the Dead with Yama's trial and the audience with Hinekora.

name: Ezomyr
summary: Ezomyte homeland on a landmass west of the Wraeclastian mainland (with the Isles of Skothe), later largely wiped out by a plague; Ogham forests in PoE2 Act 1.

name: The Fathomless Depths
summary: Underwater endgame area explored via a Bathysphere and Allflame lanterns; a pit of deathly light lies below.

name: Fellshrine Ruins
summary: Ruined former Freesia Cathedral area of Wraeclast, above the Forbidden Sanctum; Eramir calls the Fellshrine a shadow of what was once good in Wraeclast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sanctum_league", "locator": "'==Lore==' (Sanctum beneath the Fellshrine Ruins)"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_7QuY96FyhG4", "locator": "[1:51]-[2:15] Freesia Cathedral / Archbishop Joffrey"}]

name: The Forbidden Sanctum
summary: Ancient Templar enclave/ossuary-library beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, four floors deep, abandoned for a long time and now controlled by Lycia, who lures treasure hunters in through portals; floors shift from tidy library to Scourge-infested crypt.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sanctum_league", "locator": "'==Lore==': 'ancient Templar enclave hidden beneath the Fellshrine Ruins'"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_7QuY96FyhG4", "locator": "[4:05]-[4:30] four floors, library to crypt; [10:35]-[11:30] ossuary and pact"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_order_of_the_templar", "locator": "Sanctum league paragraph"}]

name: The Forest Encampment
summary: Former Azmeri/exile village taken over by Ralakesh through Greust; located between the Ashen Fields and the Northern Forest in Act 7.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_2", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_master_of_a_million_faces", "locator": "Ralakesh is located in The Forest Encampment"}]

name: Forge of the Titans
summary: Primeval forge reached through Primeval Remnants during Crucible league, where equipment trees are combined; the stone body and voice of the Molten One, the last known Titan, can be met there.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_molten_one", "locator": "NPC infobox / Lore"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_crucible_league", "locator": "'==League Mechanic==' Primeval Remnant / Forge of the Titans"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_god", "locator": "Molten One entry: 'During Crucible league, his stone body and voice can be encountered in the Forge of the Titans'"}]

name: The Grand Architect's Temple
summary: Delve node in the Vaal Outpost biome housing the boss Ahuatotli, the Blind.

name: The Grim Tangle
summary: Overgrown sinkholes beneath Ogham leading to the Count's grave past the Memorial Gate.

name: The Halani Gates
summary: Gates to the Maraketh city of Deshar; Jamanra locks them; a sandstorm blocks the road after the first battle at the gates.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest log 'Talk to Asala about the closed Gates'"}]

name: The Halls of the Dead
summary: Karui afterlife created by Hinekora before the Slumbering of the Gods as a place for Karui souls; where fallen chieftains reside and the Trial of the Ancestors is held.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_hinekora", "locator": "'==Lore==' last paragraph"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_ancestor_league", "locator": "'==Items==' (portal to the Halls of the Dead)"}]

name: Heart of the Tribe
summary: Ngakanu's sacred core with the Meeting House (Words of Akoya) and the Act 4 final boss arena where Tavakai is fought.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "map: Heart of the Tribe, Act Boss Tavakai"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Words of Akoya"}]

name: The High Gardens
summary: Act 8 gardens associated with Izaro, where Yugul lurks.

name: Highgate
summary: Mountain region where Veruso buried the virtue gems ('Tears of Maji'), where slaves mined them under Chitus, where Malachai placed the Rapture Device and the Beast lies beneath, and where a Maraketh tribe lives in PoE1.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Slave trade', 'Reign of Voll'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_sin", "locator": "'The Beast'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_4", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_9", "locator": "intro"}]

name: Holten
summary: Ezomyte holding of Thane Wulfric and Lady Elswyth, behind the Blackwood; centre of the Curse of Holten.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_recruit_the_ezomytes", "locator": "Enter Holten / Defeat the Thane and Lady"}, {"source_id": "src_web_poe2db_act6", "locator": "area list: Holten, Holten Estate"}]

name: Hunting Grounds
summary: Act 1 area beyond the clan graves that Una directs the Exile through toward Ogham Village.

name: Infested Barrens
summary: Area where the stone altar needs a large Soul Core to open the Matlan Waterways.

name: Isle of Kin
summary: Act 4 island with the Volcanic Warrens; boss The Blind Beast and Krutog, Lord of Kin. Doomed Mine holds Niko's Feverish Writings.

name: Isles of Skothe
summary: Landmass west of Sarn named with Ezomyr as the origin of the Ezomytes.

name: Jiquani's Machinarium
summary: Unlooted Vaal facility in the Chimeral Wetlands holding a large Soul Core in Jiquani's Sanctum, needed to run the Matlan Waterways.

name: Jiquani's Sanctum
summary: Deep chamber with generators and the large Soul Core, guarded by Zicoatl.

name: Kalguur
summary: Homeland of the Kalguur people in Middengard, a distant continent southeast/east of Wraeclast; not directly accessible but referenced by Expedition and Settlers of Kalguur.

name: Kaom's Stronghold
summary: Karui stronghold within the Beast where Kaom is fought.

name: The Karui Fortress
summary: Act 6 area containing Tukohama's Keep, where the Karui war god is fought.

name: Karui Shores
summary: Epilogue hub leading to the Atlas of Worlds.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_a_call_to_arms", "locator": "Upon entering Karui Shores talk to Helena"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_campaign", "locator": "Epilogue leads to Karui Shores"}]

name: Kedge Bay and Journey's End
summary: Fog-covered island whose Karui totems keep Tangmazu (appearing as Freya Hartlin) imprisoned; its fog disrupts Kingsmarch trade.

name: Keth
summary: Ancient Maraketh city and trade empire at the meeting of seven rivers, called the 'glory of the world'; ruins form an Act 2 area in PoE2.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Maraketh > Keth"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_keth", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_city_of_seven_waters", "locator": "Walkthrough 'Use the Desert Map to travel to Keth'"}]

name: The Khari Bazaar
summary: Interlude 2 settlement where Risu gives the Clearing the Way quest.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_clearing_the_way", "locator": "Quest infobox: 'Speak to Risu at the Khari Bazaar'"}]

name: Khari Crossing
summary: Desert crossing near the Khari Bazaar in PoE2 Interlude 2; the far end is plagued by Akthi and Anundr.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_clearing_the_way", "locator": "Quest log: 'Travel to the Khari Crossing' and 'The way is plagued by a great scorpion and a massive sandworm'"}]

name: Kingsmarch
summary: Kalguuran harbour town on Ngamakanui, hub of Act 4 where the Exile hires the Aurora May. Founded in PoE1's Settlers of Kalguur; Tujen says they first picked the spot to stash supplies and 'now it's going to be a city'. In the epilogue its ruins are revisited by Dannig and Makoru.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kingsmarch", "locator": "intro + '==NPCs=='; Trivia 'Act 4 town in Path of Exile 2'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "Progression table"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_1U2bFh1V9Mo", "locator": "[4:34-4:49] Tujen on Kingsmarch"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalguur", "locator": "intro: Kingsmarch harbour for settlers"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_grand_expedition", "locator": "Travel to Ruins of Kingsmarch"}]

name: Korathin
summary: Capital of Trarthus, declared by Ixan Keita in 872 IC and built by his slaves.

name: Lake of Kalandra
summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars in primordial Wraeclast where Kalandra is trapped. The league version was a mirror-realm assembled from a Mirrored Tablet and was not added to the core game.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore > Ancient Etchings"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > The Lake of Kalandra"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra_league", "locator": "League Mechanic and note on core game"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'The Lake of Kalandra'"}]

name: The Lich's Tomb
summary: Delve node of the Azurite Mine, found in the Abyssal City biome at depth 90+; it always contains the boss fight with Kurgal, the Blackblooded in the Abyssal Sanctum. The boss room is no longer accessible in a new instance after the kill.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lich_s_tomb", "locator": "Intro: 'It can only appeared in 90+ depths in the Abyssal City biome ... it always contains the boss fight with Kurgal, the Blackblooded'; 'After the boss fight has been finished, the node can be revisited'"}]

name: Lioneye's Watch
summary: Southern Eternal garrison commanded by General Marceus Lioneye, taken by Kaom's Karui in the Purity Rebellion; later the survivors' town in PoE1 Acts 1 and 6.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Lioneye's Watch' section"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_1", "locator": "lead paragraph"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_6", "locator": "Lioneye's Watch is the Act 6 town"}]

name: Lira Vaal / Atziri's Temple
summary: Royal temple of Atziri and Vaal capital for much of its history; rebuilt by Xipocado and Doryani as a self-reconstructing marvel. PoE2 Fate of the Vaal league lets players modify its layout.

name: The Lord's Labyrinth
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "1317 IC (Eternal Empire); PoE1 Act 1 quest", "story_order": null}
summary: A labyrinth built by Emperor Izaro in 1317 IC as a test to choose his successor, opened on the second Galvano of Azmeri. Chitus won it by betraying Weylin, and later sealed Izaro inside. In PoE1 it is the Act 1 quest that leads to the Trials of Ascendancy.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'The Lord's Labyrinth'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lord_s_labyrinth_quest_", "locator": "quest page"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'Reign of Izaro' and 'The Lord's Labyrinth'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_lords_labyrinth_quest", "locator": "infobox and summary"}]

name: The Lunaris Temple
summary: Temple on west side of Sarn, Piety's laboratory filled with miscreations.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_piety", "locator": "In Path of Exile"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_lunar_eclipse", "locator": "Maramoa on The Dusk and the Moon Orb"}]

name: Maligaro's Sanctum
summary: A map-like area in Act 7 entered through portals opened with Maligaro's Map from the Chamber of Sins; the Artist Maligaro and his pet spider Black Death are fought here.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_essence_of_the_artist", "locator": "Walkthrough: 'You have opened the portals using his Map, now enter Maligaro's Sanctum.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_web_of_secrets", "locator": "Walkthrough: 'Maligaro's Sanctum is a map-like area. Player consumes one portal to enter the area'"}]

name: The Matlan Waterways
summary: Vaal canal system whose controls, powered by a large Soul Core, drain the lake to reveal Utzaal.

name: Mawdun Mine
summary: Abandoned Faridun foundry guarded by Rudja, the Dread Engineer.

name: Mawdun Quarry
summary: Faridun camp where the Countess had Jamanra's followers prepare weapons and the Dreadnought.

name: Memory Nexus
summary: Hub area of Synthesis where captured Fragmented Memories are placed to form paths to rewards, enhancements and boss memories.

name: Merveil's Lair
summary: Act 1 boss area at the end of the Cavern of Anger.

name: Middengard
summary: Distant continent south-east of Wraeclast on which Kalguur lies.

name: The Molten Vault
summary: Act 3 vault marked by monkey statues of Kamasa, cleared for treasure in the Treasures of Utzaal quest; its boss is Mektul, the Forgemaster.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_treasures_of_utzaal", "locator": "Lead: 'entrance to the Molten Vault' and '===Enter The Molten Vault===' quest log"}]

name: Monastery of the Keepers
summary: Southern Atlas site; hidden chamber houses the Dreamer; Genesis Tree and Grasping Orchid located here.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_into_the_breach", "locator": "Visit the Monastery of the Keepers"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_keepers_league", "locator": "League content"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_dreamer", "locator": "hidden area in the Monastery of the Keepers"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_vruun_marshal_of_xesht", "locator": "Monastery of the Keepers to grow a Grasping Orchid"}]

name: Moti Aro
summary: Karui port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

name: Mount Kriar and the Cuachic Vault
summary: Most isolated peak of the Azmeri Ranges; its summit Cuachic Vault holds Doryani's sealed Vaal reserves.

name: Mount Veruso
summary: Mountain beneath which virtue gems were discovered by the Vaal, who used them to gain great power.

name: Mud Burrow
summary: Act 1 underground burrow reached from Clearfell, home of the Devourer; also the Abyss-linked passage in Cracks in the Earth.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_treacherous_ground", "locator": "Lead: 'a quest in the act 1 area Mud Burrow'; walkthrough '===Find the Mud Burrow==='"}]

name: The Mud Flats (Act 6)
summary: Act 6 area reached from the Coast; its entrance is blocked by Hiveborn structures until the Into the Breach quest is started.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_into_the_breach", "locator": "Walkthrough: 'approaching the entrance to the Mud Flats from the Coast in Act 6, where the entrance is blocked off by Hiveborn structures'"}]

name: Ngakanu
summary: Tukohama-tribe settlement under Chieftain Tavakai, reached late in Act 4; a hostile Blood Fever zone after Tavakai's declaration. Kaimana lives here.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kingsmarch", "locator": "Shipping: Exclusive rewards / Table of rewards"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tribal_medicine", "locator": "Explore Ngakanu / Speak to Kaimana"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Tavakai's Declaration"}]

name: Ngamakanui
summary: Karui homeland, an archipelago southwest of Lioneye's Watch; to the Karui the name (Nga + Makanui, 'the Karui Way') denotes anywhere the Karui roam. Explorable in PoE2 Act 4, where it is overrun by the Flesh Scourge (speculative per wiki).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_ngamakanui", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Karui: Kahuturoa 'Ngamakanui'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Lioneye's Watch' subsection"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kitava_s_torments", "locator": "Lani dialogue"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_1U2bFh1V9Mo", "locator": "[5:33] Kahuturoa: 'Ngamakanui isn't a place, not really.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Doryani"}]

name: Ogham
summary: Forest region where the PoE2 campaign opens; Count Geonor rules it from Ogham Manor and the Ezomytes live under his terror.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_lore", "locator": "Prelude > Count Geonor; Act 1 section"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_recruit_the_ezomytes", "locator": "Speak to Renly"}]

name: Ogham Farmlands
summary: Act 1 farmland area near Ogham Village where Una's family hut, and her lute, are found.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_lost_lute", "locator": "Tips: 'Una's family hut is south and slightly east of the waypoint'; walkthrough '===Search for Una's Lute==='"}]

name: Ogham Manor
summary: Count Geonor's seat in Act 1; the Beast seed was caged in its foundations and fed by hangings.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_1", "locator": "Progression table, Ogham Manor row"}, {"source_id": "src_yt_4UKJmVK7Iv4", "locator": "[6:30]-[6:51]"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Ogham Manor items"}]

name: Ogham Village
summary: Act 1 village where the Executioner is found and the Seed of Corruption is sought.

name: Oriath
summary: Island off the south-east of Wraeclast, founded by Innocence's banished followers and ruled by the Templar theocracy from Theopolis. Unaffected by the Cataclysm, it served as the Empire's successor; destroyed in the Atlas storyline of PoE1 and revisited in PoE2 Act 4.

name: Oriath Docks
summary: Act 10 town where Lani, Weylam and Lilly Roth, Divinia and Sin base themselves.

name: Oriath Square
summary: Square leading to the Templar Courts, Ossuary and Reliquary.

name: Overseer's Tower
summary: Act 5 town, rebel camp.

name: The Pale Court
summary: Prophecy-system area where the Pale Council bosses (Eber, Inya, Yriel, Volkuur) are fought; the wiki states this content was removed in 3.17.0.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eber_the_plaguemaw", "locator": "Infobox location = [[The Pale Court]]; header 'The prophecy system was removed from the game in version 3.17.0'"}]

name: Path of Mourning
summary: Route through Deshar that leads the Exile to the Faridun at the Spires.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trail_of_corruption_act_2", "locator": "Quest log 'Travel through the Path of Mourning'"}]

name: The Patriarch and Matriarch Halls
summary: Two Precursor halls visited in Legacy of the Precursors; the Exile defeats Phyx, Sentinel of the Spark, and Phya, Sentinel of the Cradle, to recover the Origin Spark and Origin Cradle.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest log (hidden comment block) steps 112-128: 'Travel to the Patriarch Halls', 'Defeat Phyx, Sentinel of the Spark', 'Defeat Phya, Sentinel of the Cradle'"}]

name: Phaaryl
summary: Unexplorable location north of Sarn, said to be the point of invasion of the Harbingers as described in Commander Kirac's 'Kirac's Memory' quest dialogue. More than three thousand Oriathan soldiers were killed in the Battle of Phaaryl.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_phaaryl", "locator": "lead paragraph: 'an unexplorable location north of Sarn ... the point of invasion by the Harbingers, as described by Commander Kirac's Kirac's Memory quest dialogue. Over three thousand Oriathan soldiers were killed in the Battle of Phaaryl'"}]

name: Phrecia (imperial heartlands)
summary: Imperial heartlands of the Eternal Empire named in honour of General Alano Phrecia after he drove away a pervasive darkness; contains Phrecia Cathedral (modern Fellshrine Ruins).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "Reign of Alano Phrecia"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Reign of Alano Phrecia"}]

name: Phrecia Cathedral
summary: Cathedral seat of Archbishop Geofri in the Phrecian heartlands (today the Fellshrine Ruins); Geofri was killed here by Maligaro.

name: Plunder's Point
summary: Island unlocked via the Torn Map Pieces of The Runeseeker; abandoned Kalguuran post (Cadigan the Wise's notes) and an Expedition encounter.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_runeseeker", "locator": "Rewards: unlocks Plunder's Point"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Cadigan the Wise; Terrible Fate"}]

name: Pondium
summary: Kalguuran port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

name: Pondium (Valerie's home port)
summary: Lawless port where Valerie and Vesper grew up; Valerie says it holds more fairness than Oriath.

name: Precursor Shrine
summary: Underground shrine built around a mirror by the 'oldest of men' (probably primeval/precursor); Uhtred hid here and the Kalguuran survivors tried to reach it. No link to Kalandra's mirror is proven.

name: Precursor Towers
summary: Precursor Tower system met on the PoE2 Atlas, apparently built for terraforming Wraeclast (per Doryani's research quoted on the History page). In Legacy of the Precursors, activating a Precursor Beacon makes a Precursor Fortress rise from the ground; the Ziggurat sits over ancient 'leylines'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Precursor civilization"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tower", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_grand_project", "locator": "flavour: 'they sought to master this world'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Activate the Precursor Beacon: 'the Precursor Fortress will rise from the ground'; Doryani on leylines"}]

name: Prisoner's Gate (Act 6)
summary: Act 6 area with the side area Valley of the Fire Drinker where Abberath is found.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_abberath_the_cloven_one", "locator": "Located in The Valley of the Fire Drinker, side area of Prisoner's Gate"}]

name: Qimah
summary: Maraketh city where the Gifting of Water is held; Qimah Reservoir is Azmadi's arena.

name: The Red Vale
summary: Act 1 vale of battle debris where three Obelisks of Rust hold Runes of Power.

name: Riben Fell
summary: Kalguuran port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

name: The Riverbank
summary: Act 1 starting area where the Exile washes up after escaping execution; the Bloated Miller is the area boss and the Reaching Clearfell quest starts here.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_1", "locator": "Act 1 intro and Progression table (The Riverbank, boss: The Bloated Miller)"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_reaching_clearfell", "locator": "quest 'Reaching Clearfell' is a quest in the act 1 area The Riverbank"}]

name: The Rogue Harbour
summary: Hub town of the criminal guild known as the Ring, reached by a Rogue's Marker portal (introduced by an Act 6 quest from 3.13.0); home of the fence Faustus, administrator Kurai, rogues and the Wayfinder Adiyah who opens contract portals.

name: Ruins of Kingsmarch
summary: Devastated Kingsmarch, hub of the Expedition storyline.

name: Sandswept Marsh
summary: Marsh crossed in search of the Ziggurat that marks the sunken city.

name: Sarn
summary: Capital of the Eternal Empire, founded by Veruso on the site of Azala Vaal. Burned during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons, rebuilt, besieged by Voll in 1334 IC and fallen within an hour of the Cataclysm. The Act 8 city of the exile.

name: The Sarn Encampment
summary: Act 8 town amid the ruins of Sarn; home of Hargan, Clarissa and Maramoa.

name: Sceptre of God
summary: Imperial palace tower of Sarn where Chitus, Malachai and Dialla held court (concubines kept there); the exile kills Dominus atop it in Act 3.

name: The Shaper's Realm
summary: Realm at the centre of the Atlas where the Shaper is fought ('the Crucible' in the legacy quest); the Uber Elder fight takes place in its version of the Absence of Value and Meaning.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_elder_quest", "locator": "The Uber Elder section"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_shaper_quest", "locator": "Assignment 11: 'found the Shaper in the Crucible'"}]

name: Shrike Island
summary: Act 4 island where Karui youths take the Test of Might; boss Scourge of the Skies.

name: The Slave Pens
summary: Arrival area in Oriath ruled by Overseer Krow.

name: Solaris Temple
summary: Sarn temple where Malachai built the Rapture Device over more than a year; the exile meets Dialla on Level 2 in Act 3.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_eternal_empire", "locator": "'Reign of Voll'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_gemling_queen", "locator": "Walkthrough"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_solar_eclipse", "locator": "Maramoa on The Dawn and the Sun Orb"}]

name: Starfall Crater
summary: Area reached through an entrance that can randomly appear in ore-deposit maps; holds The Black Knight, who guards several Verisium Outcrops (Kingsmarch wiki, Bosses section).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kingsmarch", "locator": "==Bosses== ===The Black Knight===: \"Map areas containing ore deposits can randomly contain an entrance to the Starfall Crater, which holds the Black Knight inside guarding several Verisium Outcrops.\""}]

name: Stridevolf
summary: Enclave on the southern outskirts of the Vastiri Plains, past Mount Vastiri. It was burned down by the unnamed 'bandit king of Stridevolf' during a conflict with the Maraketh warrior Orbala. Governor Kastov is listed among its notable members.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_stridevolf", "locator": "lead paragraph: 'an enclave on the southern outskirts of the Vastiri Plains, past Mount Vastiri ... burned down by the bandit king of Stridevolf during a conflict with Maraketh warrior Orbala'; 'Notable members: Governor Kastov'. No date is given on the page, so era is unknown."}]

name: The Submerged Passage
summary: Flooded tidal cave in the Act 1 Mud Flats, behind the glyph wall. It is drained when the three Karui glyphs are fitted into the wall.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_breaking_some_eggs", "locator": "Quest objective 'open the Submerged Passage'; 'The Submerged Passage is now open'"}]

name: Sulphur Vents (Delve)
summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) with Fractured, Metallic, Perfect, Aetheric and Encrusted fossils; its biome-specific nodes include Humid Fissure and Restless Rubble. Introduced in 3.4.0.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sulphur_vents_delve", "locator": "Intro: 'Sulfur Vents is one of the biomes of the Azurite Mine'; Fossils list; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game'"}]

name: Tane's Laboratory
summary: Underground laboratory of Tane Octavius near the Karui Shores, undamaged by Oriath's destruction; where Metamorph work is done.

name: Te Onui
summary: Karui port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

name: The Templar Courts
summary: Templar stronghold built by Avarius's command; becomes Torched Courts.

name: Temple of Chaos
summary: Vaal temple near the outskirts of Utzaal where commoners could attempt the Trials of Chaos to become high priests; in PoE2 Act 3, off the Chimeral Wetlands.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_chaos_lore", "locator": "paragraph on the Temple of Chaos"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_trial_of_chaos", "locator": "Access"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "section 'Chaos'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_3", "locator": "progression table"}]

name: The Temple of Decay
summary: Arakaali's temple in the Vaal City where Silk is lost and Arakaali is killed.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_mother_of_spiders", "locator": "Kill Arakaali at the heart of the Temple of Decay"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "Arakaali"}]

name: Temple of Kopec
summary: Sealed Vaal sun-god temple beneath the Ziggurat Encampment, guarded by Ketzuli; houses the time gateway used to travel to Utzaal's past.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest log 'Enter the Temple of Kopec'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "quest log"}]

name: The Abyss (place)
summary: Underground realm reached through Abyss pits; Abyssal Depths.

name: The Aqueduct
summary: Act 4 area on the way to Highgate, where Lady Dialla first waits for the Exile to ask them to destroy the Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_eternal_nightmare", "locator": "Walkthrough quest log: 'Dialla is waiting for you on the Aqueduct'"}]

name: The Ascent
summary: Mt. Veruso path east of Highgate (an Act 4 area, level 40) leading to the Resonator whose portal opens to Oriath.

name: The Bath House
summary: Sarn area where Hector Titucius guards the Wings of Vastiri.

name: The Battlefront
summary: Sarn battlefront held by the Ebony Legion. A Blackguard chest here holds the Ribbon Spool, guarded by an optional boss.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ribbon_spool", "locator": "Walkthrough: 'Find the Ribbon Spool in the Battlefront'"}]

name: The Beachhead
summary: The Beachhead is a map (several variants, e.g. Red tier and Infused) that holds the Harbinger Portal; defeating the final King Harbinger in any variant drops the unique Harbinger item pieces.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_harbinger", "locator": "'Unique pieces' and 'Harbinger scroll' sections; src_poewiki_harbinger_league 'Unique items' section"}]

name: The Belly of the Beast / Rotting Core (Act 9)
summary: Interior of the Beast's corpse; the Black Core / Rotting Core is where the Depraved Trinity is fought.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_recurring_nightmare", "locator": "Enter the Black Core"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_depraved_trinity", "locator": "Location: The Rotting Core"}]

name: The Black Cathedral
summary: Level-80 area off the Well of Souls entered only with Kulemak's Invitation; site of the Kulemak encounter.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_2", "locator": "area table: The Black Cathedral 80 - Kulemak's Invitation"}]

name: The Breach (realm)
summary: Parallel realm opened by breaches in which Breachlords hold domains; see concept_breach.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_breach_league", "locator": "lead: breaches open a parallel realm containing otherworldly monsters"}]

name: The Bridge Encampment
summary: Act 7 town on the broken bridge once ruled by Kraityn, now home to Yeena, Helena, Eramir and Weylam Roth's ghost.

name: The Burning Monolith
summary: Site where the Arbiter of Ash is fought; in 0.1-0.4 a door on the Atlas opened by three Crisis Fragments, in 0.5 moved inside the Precursor Fortress.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_pinnacle_of_flame", "locator": "Find The Burning Monolith"}, {"source_id": "src_web_game8_arbiter_of_ash", "locator": "Three Crisis Fragments, one from each Citadel, open the Burning Monolith"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "steps 100-105"}]

name: The Canals
summary: The Act 10 waterways of Oriath, behind Kitava's Horns, where Kitava feeds; Innocence opens the way to them and the Feeding Trough lies there.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_an_end_to_hunger", "locator": "Walkthrough: 'Kitava, the Insatiable's Horns block the way to the The Canals where Kitava, the Insatiable feeds.'"}]

name: The Cradle
summary: Mirror-portal realm near the Beast where Atziri, the Fell Serpent is fought in PoE2.

name: The Crematorium
summary: Slum area where Piety tortured Tolman.

name: The Desecrated Chambers
summary: Defiled Chamber of Innocence where Avarius' staff lies; Avarius, Reassembled is fought here.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_death_and_rebirth", "locator": "desecrated Chamber of Innocence"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_avarius_reassembled", "locator": "Location: The Desecrated Chambers"}]

name: The Dread Thicket
summary: An Act 7 area in the Northern Forest where the Fireflies needed for Yeena's Fire Dew are found.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_lighting_the_way", "locator": "Walkthrough: 'Search for the Firefly in the The Dread Thicket (Act 7), then deliver Firefly to Yeena.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_7", "locator": "Progression table: 'The Dread Thicket (Act 7) 53' branching from The Northern Forest (Act 7)"}]

name: The Dreadnought
summary: Faridun war caravan carrying the Beast across the Vastiri; the Act 2 boss is fought on it.

name: The Dried Lake
summary: Place where Voll fled after the Cataclysm and wrote his Confession; he and his undead legion remained there for centuries.

name: The Excavation
summary: Twilight Order dig site on Arastas, boss Benedictus; leads to the Excavated Site whose murals depict the Weapon and the Beast and where the Weapon is reforged.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_4", "locator": "The Excavation: Benedictus"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'"}]

name: The Feeding Trough
summary: Final area of Act 10 where Kitava feeds and is slain.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_an_end_to_hunger", "locator": "You have found Kitava at his Feeding Trough"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_10", "locator": "Progression"}]

name: The Grain Gate
summary: Sarn gate attacked by the Purity forces; failed assault repelled by Chitus' gemlings. Gemlings survive there in Act 8.

name: The Grand Arena
summary: Daresso's Dream arena modelled on Theopolis's Grand Arena.

name: The Grelwood
summary: Act 1 forest containing the Tree of Souls that binds the Hooded One.

name: The Harbour Bridge
summary: Sarn bridge with the Sky Shrine where Solaris and Lunaris are summoned and killed.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_solaris_and_lunaris", "locator": "Sky Shrine in the center of The Harbour Bridge"}]

name: The Library
summary: Sarn library where Siosa dwells; Archives hide the Golden Pages.

name: The Lightless Hollow
summary: Circular arena with a central abyssal pit where Zorath lies suspended; accessible directly on the Atlas.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_zorath_vile_assembled", "locator": "Entry: \"Zorath's arena is called The Lightless Hollow, and can be directly traversed to on the Atlas\""}]

name: The Menagerie
summary: Act 2 location unlocked by completing Einhar's Hunt; Einhar gives the optional Einhar's Menagerie quest here (perform beastcrafting once).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_einhar_s_hunt", "locator": "Rewards and 'Quest Complete - You have unlocked the Menagerie'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_einhar_s_menagerie", "locator": "'Walkthrough': 'You have unlocked the Menagerie'"}]

name: The Mines (Highgate)
summary: Mountain mines sealed by Deshret with the Beast inside.

name: The Necropolis
summary: Graveyard where haunted corpses are buried and exorcised to add crafting modifiers to the Tome of Arimor.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_necropolis_league", "locator": "'==League mechanic=='"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_undertaker_s_apprentice", "locator": "Perform the Exorcism in The Necropolis"}]

name: The Nightmare (Scourge realm)
summary: Ruined, demon-infested alternate version of Wraeclast the exile shifts into in Scourge; monsters there become the new Beyond monsters. Not the same as the Vaal 'crimson nightmare' realm of Atziri.

name: The Oasis
summary: Hidden oasis where Shakari rebuilds her army; she is fought in the Sand Pit.

name: The Origin Tower
summary: Precursor tower reached via the Waygate in the Epilogue; the Exile places the Origin Core at the top, where Tecrod intervenes and the Arbiter of Divinity is fought.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tecrod", "locator": "area: the Burning Monolith, the Origin Tower"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "steps 108-141"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tecrod", "locator": "Lore"}]

name: The Ossuary (Act 10)
summary: Templar bone-vault in Oriath holding Atziri's Elixir of Allure (love potion in her lover's skull) and the Mortinomicon Exitio Immortalis.

name: The Precursor Fortress
summary: Vast Precursor structure that rises from the ground when the first Precursor Beacon is activated (0.5); contains the Ancient/Western/Eastern Gateways, Enigma Chambers, the Burning Monolith, the Halls and the Origin Tower. Official 0.5.0 notes: 'The Cataclysm of the Beast has invoked an ancient protocol'; players seek keys to reach and disarm ancient Precursor weapons.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Activate the Precursor Beacon: Fortress will rise from the ground"}, {"source_id": "src_web_domistae_poe2_endgame_guide", "locator": "Fortress: Origins of Divinity (Storyline I)"}, {"source_id": "src_ggg_content_update_0_5_0", "locator": "Origins of Divinity: ancient protocol; obtain keys to reach the Precursor weapons and disarm them"}]

name: The Quarry
summary: Act 9 area with a side area for Garukhan and the blood pools around the Lesion where Sin burns a way into the Beast.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ruler_of_highgate", "locator": "Travel to The Quarry"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_recurring_nightmare", "locator": "Sin: meet at the Quarry"}]

name: The Quay
summary: Sarn dockside where Clarissa's failed resurrection of Tolman takes place.

name: The Ravaged Square
summary: Oriath's square where Kitava's Horns block the way to the Canals.

name: The Reliquary
summary: Holds Kitava's Torments.

name: The Sacred Grove
summary: Ancient garden carved from the land (possibly by ancestral Azmeri, 'older than the Eternal Empire') where Oshabi plants seeds; restored her connection to the land.

name: The Sewers
summary: Filthy tunnels under the river between Sarn's districts, filled with the Undying. An Undying Blockade bars the way and is burned away with Infernal Talc.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_fiery_dust", "locator": "Walkthrough: 'Approach the Undying Blockade in The Sewers'"}]

name: The Ship Graveyard
summary: Coastal wreck field where Fairgraves is marooned.

name: The Simulacrum
summary: The Simulacrum: a wave-based Delirium encounter opened by the Simulacrum map fragment in a Map Device; the fragment is crafted from Simulacrum Splinters dropped by Delirium monsters.

name: Slums and Grand Arena (Oriath)
summary: Named on the PoE2 wiki as the progression areas of Act 5; datamined further areas: Gardens, Den of Pleasure, Pantheon of the Forsaken Gods. Unreleased.

name: The Temple of Atzoatl
summary: Vaal temple-complex built in the last years of Atziri's reign, centre of trade, mechanical research, Chayula worship and Doryani's gem experiments; Atziri moved her seat here. PoE1 Incursion league lets players reach it 2,000 years in the past.

name: The Vaal City
summary: Vaal city risen from the depths in Act 7, accessed via the Causeway; contains Arakaali's Temple of Decay.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_lighting_the_way", "locator": "Yeena in The Vaal City near Arakaali's temple"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_no_time_like_the_present", "locator": "city has risen from the depths"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vaal", "locator": "Reign of Queen Tetzlapokal"}]

name: The Weaver's Chambers
summary: Spider-infested caves entered from the Western Forest.

name: The Wetlands (Act 2)
summary: Act 2 wetland area where the great tree Lorrata has rooted itself across the entrance to the Vaal Ruins. The Exile poisons the tree with Maligaro's Spike and the Baleful Gem.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_root_of_the_problem", "locator": "Quest objective 'Poison the tree, Lorrata, in The Wetlands'"}]

name: The Wetlands (Act 6)
summary: Act 6 area whose side area The Spawning Ground holds Ryslatha.

name: Theopolis
summary: Capital city of the Theocracy of Oriath; site of the Oriath academy where Valdo worked and of the Templar Laboratory.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "'Oriath' and 'Daresso and Merveil'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_shaper_quest", "locator": "Memory of Wonder: 'a map of Theopolis'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Valdo Caeserius"}]

name: Throne of Atziri
summary: Tier-3 incursion room of Xipocado in the Temple of Atzoatl containing a boss encounter with Atziri.

name: The Titan Grotto
summary: Grotto beneath the Valley of the Titans where Zalmarath guards the Flame Ruby.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_a_crown_of_stone", "locator": "Walkthrough 'Find a way into the Titan Grotto'"}]

name: Traitor's Passage
summary: Hidden tunnel leading to the top of the Halani Gates, where Balbala is sealed as a Djinn.

name: Trarthus
summary: Region southwest of Wraeclast and west of the Karui archipelago; capital Korathin; a brutal slave-and-killer culture ruled by four Great Houses, once the Eternal Empire's dumping ground for exiles.

name: Tsoatha
summary: Ancient sunken city, domain of the Brine King; Lilly Roth wants to plunder it after his death.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_map_to_tsoatha", "locator": "Lilly: 'his sunken domain, the ancient city of Tsoatha'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_brine_king_quest", "locator": "Sin: 'ruins of Tsoatha'"}]

name: The Twilight Strand
summary: The shore where each PoE1 league's Exile washes up after the Oriathan sentence, face-down in the sand.

name: Utzaal
summary: Vaal city, centre of Doryani's research, drowned by its own waterways at the Cataclysm to spite looters. PoE2 Act 3 setting: the Exile drains the Sunken City, then travels to its living past.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_3", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "Quest logs 'Speak to the Hooded One' / 'Enter Utzaal in the past'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act_3", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_vaal", "locator": "quest log"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Vaal fall: waterways drowning"}]

name: The Vaal Ruins (PoE1 Act 2)
summary: Vaal ruin from which the Exile unleashes Darkness.

name: Vaal Ruins (PoE2)
summary: Endgame hub in PoE2 east/north-east of the Atlas start with a waypoint and Temple Console for Atziri's Temple.

name: Vaal Temple (map)
summary: Atlas map area themed on Vaal corruption, containing ten Vaal Vessel strongboxes and the demon boss trio; tileset similar to the Apex of Sacrifice.

name: Vastiri (Plains / Desert)
summary: Region bordering Phaaryl, Lira Vaal and Sarn, home of the Maraketh; once a lush land of forests and seven rivers around Keth, it became a desert over thousands of years after the Beast silenced the gods.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_vastiri_plains", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "The Maraketh paragraphs 1-3"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_queen_of_the_sands", "locator": "Sin on the oasis storm"}]

name: The Venom Crypts
summary: Act 3 crypt area containing the Den of the Serpent Priestess, where the Corpse-snake Venom quest item is found.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_slithering_dead", "locator": "Quest lead: 'explore the area to find the landmark Den of the Serpent Priestess'"}]

name: The Well of Souls
summary: Wellspring of necromancy that collects all souls; Kulemak's seat. In PoE2 reached via the Lightless Passage from Mastodon Badlands in Act 2; later the Abyss hub.

name: Whakapanu Island
summary: Lush Act 4 island whose Karui carvings tell of settlers repeatedly vanishing into the Singing Caverns, where the Siren Diamora hunts; boss Great White One.

name: The Withered Willow
summary: Delirium hub on the 0.5 Atlas, south-west of the starting point.

name: Wraeclast
summary: The continent on which the Exile's story takes place; PoE2 is set on (and expands) Wraeclast, while Oriath is another continent seen in PoE1.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro and Prehistory"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_wraeclast", "locator": "intro"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "intro; section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_1", "locator": "lead"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_act_6", "locator": "returns to Wraeclast"}]

name: Ziggurat Encampment
summary: Treasure hunter camp built atop a ziggurat in a lake; unknowingly sits on the time gateway. Town hub of PoE2 Act 3.

name: Ziggurat Refuge
summary: Where the Exile unintentionally ends up instead of Oriath; Doryani's Ziggurat above Precursor leylines holds the Waygate/Map Device.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_siege_of_oriath", "locator": "Quest Complete"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Speak to Doryani: leylines, Waygate"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Take a Waystone from Doryani in The Ziggurat Refuge"}]

name: Aberrations
summary: Environmental lore objects tied to the Originator (Zana) and her father Valdo. Most entries are narrated by Zana: the Atlas as a trap, Sirus's transformation by the Atlas, her intervention through memory threads to save him, and the Templars' brutality. The entries in the Incarnation boss arenas are narrated by Valdo.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_aberration", "locator": "lead: 'environmental lore objects found in areas related to Zana, the Originator ... the ones in the Incarnation boss arenas are narrated by Valdo'; 'Entry 2 (The Success)': 'I set the threads in motion across time and space'; 'The Neglected Flame' on Sirus"}]

name: Al-Hezmin's Journals
summary: Four clickable hunter's journals from Al-Hezmin's arena. They are notes on his companions (Baran's prayers, Veritania's reading, Zana's secrets, Drox's drills), his rivalry with Drox, and a final entry about a 'New Person' who talked with Zana and seemed stronger than the other exiles.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_al_hezmin_s_journals", "locator": "section 'Journal I' (Baran: 'Prayer is the centre of his regimen'; Zana: 'Hiding something important') to 'Journal IV': 'New Person: I don't recognise this one ... Saw them talking to Zana.'"}]

name: Ancient Etchings (Kalandra)
summary: Series of Ancient Etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra herself, recounting her entrapment, scorn for gods (Etching V: a conversation with someone implied to be Sin), and the Order of the Djinn's failed rescue (Etching VI).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore > Ancient Etchings"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "Prehistory > The Lake of Kalandra footnotes"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_kalandra", "locator": "Lore: Ancient Etchings"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_environmental_lore", "locator": "Ancient Etchings entry (found throughout the Lake)"}]

name: Baran's Journals
summary: Four clickable journals from Baran's arena: a will bequeathing his staff and platemail to Veritania, Sirus, Drox and Al-Hezmin and his Oriathan home to Templar siblings; a letter to Landren about being trapped in the Atlas; a letter to a discoverer describing the demon that fed on Valdo Caeserius's memories ('the Decay') and Sirus's sacrifice; and a final entry in which Baran turns to God and plans to take the Atlas.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_baran_s_journals", "locator": "section 'Journal I' (Last Will and Testament: 'To my good friends and allies, Veritania, Sirus, Drox, and Al-Hezmin'), 'Journal III' ('feeding on the memories of Valdo Caeserius'), 'Journal IV' ('I am your sword')"}]

name: Journals of the Conquerors
summary: Lore objects in the Conquerors' arenas (added 3.9.2) narrating each Elderslayer's descent.

name: Drox's Journals
summary: Four clickable journals in Drox's arena in which the former exile pursues a kingdom of law and justice through force, conquers valley after valley and grows more convinced that strength will make the mists real, ending as 'Drox the Warlord'.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_drox_s_journals", "locator": "section 'Journal I' ('Drox the Just') to 'Journal IV' ('Drox the Warlord.'); Journal I: 'I shall be the one who leads')"}]

name: The First Edict
summary: Unexplained so far. Tecrod, hunting for the Edicts, is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity with 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'; on completing the Epilogue quest Legacy of the Precursors the log reads 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.' Its contents are not described in sources read; 'ordain' implies it is something that can be enacted or activated, and the Origin Tower / Origin Core are the setting.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tecrod", "locator": "Lore: 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "Quest Complete: 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_tecrod", "locator": "Lore: Tecrod 'hunting for the Edicts'"}]

name: The Fourth Edict
summary: Mystery edict. In Legacy of the Precursors (0.5.0) the quest-log step 'Investigate the Fourth Edict' follows the defeat of the Arbiter of Ash; its contents are not revealed in the verified sources.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_legacy_of_the_precursors", "locator": "quest step 102 'Investigate the Fourth Edict'"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_the_ezomytes", "locator": "The Great Fire: 'likely caused by the Fourth Edict, a contingency created by the Precursors to purge Wraeclast in flames'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_arbiter_of_ash", "locator": "quote 'The Fourth Edict beckons' (flaming orb attack) - reported via search result, unverified locally"}, {"source_id": "src_web_quora_fourth_edict", "locator": "fan answer: fourth edict = flame seed (speculation)"}]

name: The Second Edict
summary: Never shown directly. Only Doryani's speculation, after the Third Edict is revealed: 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict... Why would any civilisation intentionally create the Seed of Corruption?'
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict...'"}]

name: The Third Edict
summary: Precursor edict whose instrument is the Weapon. After the Hooded One reforges it, the inscription reads 'The instrument of the Third Edict'; the Weapon was 'designed for the sole purpose of cleansing Corruption... and destroying the Beast'. Revealed in Act 4 (0.3.0, whose update bears the name 'The Third Edict'). The Hooded One's wording ('that third mural') implies the edicts are murals he had seen in the Excavated Site.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_the_search", "locator": "Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural. The forging revealed an inscription. The symbols declare it The instrument of the Third Edict.'"}, {"source_id": "src_poe2wiki_act", "locator": "Version history 0.3.0: 'The instrument of the Third Edict. Journey to Kingsmarch...'"}]

name: Emperor's Warning
summary: Notice at The Prisoner's arena: 'By the order of Emperor Izaro... The prisoner within is beyond death.' signed Emperor Chitus Perandus.

name: Feverish Writings (Niko)
summary: Letter by Niko ('Your master, Niko') in the Doomed Mine on the Isle of Kin, urging miners to gather sulphite while a blind beast whispers in the dark. Continues PoE1's Niko (Delve) into PoE2.

name: Count Geonor's Edicts (Ogham decrees)
chronology: {"in_world_year": null, "relative": "~20 years after PoE1, Ogham, Act 1", "story_order": null}
summary: Notices posted across Ogham by Count Geonor declaring all crimes punishable by hanging, bodies thrown into a pit beneath his manor; a 'notice of criminality' is found near Clearfell. Not Precursor edicts; the executions fed the Beast seed/creature in the manor cage.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_yt_4UKJmVK7Iv4", "locator": "[0:25]-[0:41] 'The count's edicts posted throughout the island declared that all crimes were now punishable by hanging'; [4:25]-[4:36]"}]

name: Geonor's Journal
summary: Environmental lore in Ogham Manor: Geonor writes that Oriana 'assures me, we can right some of the wrongs of the past' and promises a way forward for Ogham, showing how the Countess recruited him.

name: Letter (Kingsmarch environmental lore)
summary: Rotating letters in the Kingsmarch tavern by Johan, Raulf, Sonja, Dannig, Rog, Tujen, Gwennen, Faustus and Isla revealing their secret rebel ties, loves and loyalties.

name: Letters from Chitus
summary: Three letters from Chitus to Cadiro (1316-1318 IC) planning to win Izaro's Labyrinth. Released as physical GGG merchandise.

name: Letters of Exile
summary: Environmental lore object in Lioneye's Watch: court papers nailed to stakes that give the sentences of named exiles (1597-1599 IC) in the formula 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. Added in version 0.10.8. Distinct from text_letters_from_chitus (Chitus's letters to Cadiro) and text_vaal_letters (Vaal victims' letters).
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_letters_of_exile", "locator": "intro: 'Letters of Exile is an environmental lore object found in Lioneye's Watch.'; section '==Format==' sentencing formula; version history 0.10.8"}]

name: Lifegiver's Manifesto
summary: Catarina's writings in Syndicate hideouts urging an immortal new world order and herself as eternal queen.

name: The Lord's Labyrinth (gamebook)
summary: An official GGG gamebook (2019) that retells the Lord's Labyrinth from Weylin's perspective. The PoE Wiki reports repeated inconsistencies with in-game sources, so it is generally not treated as canon.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_book_the_lords_labyrinth_gamebook", "locator": "gamebook forum post, 28 Oct 2019 (cited in History of Wraeclast, 'The Lord's Labyrinth')"}, {"source_id": "src_poewiki_history_of_wraeclast", "locator": "section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' (gamebook note: generally not canon)"}]

name: Lycia's relics
summary: Forbidden Sanctum relics revealing the Original Sin and Innocence's ascension.

name: Path of Exile: Origins
summary: Official comic recounting Victario, the Karui Way, the Chamber of Sins and Chitus' death.

name: Path of Exile: Origins (comic)
summary: A four-issue official comic by Grinding Gear Games and Dynamite Entertainment, told from Victario's perspective. Digital issues ran from July 2014 to April 2015; the paperback was published by Dynamite in June 2015. It centres on the Purity Rebellion and events leading up to the Cataclysm.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_book_path_of_exile_origins", "locator": "'Publication' section (issue table) and intro: written by Edwin McRae and Royal McGraw, illustrated by Carlos Rodriguez"}]

name: Precursor Edicts
summary: Vague Precursor murals depicting the Beast (or a precursor of it) and possibly instructions for containing it. The corpus separately says Sin later created the Beast from a Precursor Seed of Corruption; any reading that the Beast predates the gods is interpretation.

name: The Purity Chronicles
summary: Six-book chronicle by Garivaldi in the Library of Sarn (Act 3 area) on the Purity Rebellion.

name: Memory Fragments of the Shaper
summary: Seven in-game diary entries (Home, Intrigue, Wonder, Dream, Nightmare, Grief, Awakening) in which Valdo describes the golden device, dreams, Zana's capture and resolving to 'forge a world anew'. Partly superseded by the Book of Memories retcon.

name: Sirus' Journals
summary: Four clickable lore journals in the Conquerors of the Atlas boss rooms that expand the story of Sirus, Awakener of Worlds: his wish for purpose, his dread of the monster the group pursues, the last days with his companions, and his entrapment and 'empty' existence after he stepped into an orb of darkness.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_sirus_journals", "locator": "section 'Journal 1' ('If it weren't for Zana...') to 'Journal 4' ('They left me. In my moment of need, they left me.' ... 'Empty.')"}]

name: Chamber of Innocence stained glass windows
summary: Templar propaganda in Oriath depicting Innocence as pure and Sin as deceitful twin; later contradicted by Lycia.

name: Tavakai's Declaration
summary: In-game note found in Ngakanu: Tavakai declares the 'era of the Mighty', that the last Ngakuramakoi's body will become the new world and that 'The End of Time has come'.

name: The Ancients (Trinian)
summary: In-game history by Trinian in the Library of Sarn (PoE1 Act 3), Books 1-5 on Atziri, Zerphi, Doryani, the Azmeri and the Fall.

name: Architects' notes in Atziri's Temple
summary: Environmental texts in Atziri's Temple: 'The Perfect Design' (Architect's living-machine temple, expecting Doryani's proxies to try to stop 'Atziri's Ascension'), 'Disloyalty' (an Architect suspects Doryani is moving against the Queen over the Red Communion) and 'The Forever Queen' (Atziri names a critic her personal Architect).

name: Vaal Letters
summary: Twelve readable letters by victims and subjects of Atziri's regime, documenting sacrifice and dissent.

name: Veritania's Journals
summary: Four clickable journal entries that appeared in Veritania's arena after she was defeated. They trace her from a self-described disciplined exile who is disgusted by Atlas vice, to the self-appointed 'Redeemer' who plans to purge the mortals who indulge.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_veritania_s_journals", "locator": "section 'Journal I' to 'Journal IV': e.g. Journal III 'I am the only one that can save us', signed 'Veritania the Pure'; Journal IV 'I shall save you from your own vices by purging your weakness.' signed 'Veritania the Redeemer'"}]

name: Victario's Writings
summary: Four environmental lore texts in The Library, written as anecdotes and allegory by the poet Victario of Sarn: Kalisa Maas and the Virtue gem that shatters glass; the Blackest Monkey parable; Slaves of Virtue, on shackled workers who mine gems for the Eternal citizens while Malachai abuses them; and A Friend in Need, on the musician Lorenzi who has a gem implanted in his hand.
sources: [{"source_id": "src_poewiki_victario_s_writings", "locator": "section headings 'Volume 1: Kalisa Maas', 'Volume 2: The Blackest Monkey', 'Volume 3: Slaves of Virtue' (mentions Malachai and Highgate), 'Volume 4: A Friend in Need' (Lorenzi and Malachai's gem implant); each signed 'Victario of Sarn'"}]

name: Voll's Confession
summary: Voll's confession that he trusted the most corrupt of men.

name: The Word of the Dreamer
summary: Environmental-lore book in the Monastery of the Keepers written by Ailith recording five visions of the Dreamer. Four visions warn of the Mother (births flesh), the Red Pyre (flame/addiction), the Forked Psyche (thought without will) and the Preserved Patterns (imprisoned bodies), each of whom the Dreamer 'once knew'; the fifth says the Four have become One and that the Genesis Tree is his gift. The mapping of these four to Uul-Netol (flesh), Xoph (fire), Esh (forked thought) and Tul (preserved/frozen) is inference from epithets and the wiki's note that the book is about the four Breachlords that became Xesht.
